question: What was the real name of 'Red Fort' (Delhi) built by Shahjahan?
solution: The Red Fort is the pinnacle of Mughal architecture. It has wonderful structures like Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas and Nahar-i-Bahisht (Stream of Heaven).

question: In which year Aurangzeb became the Mughal emperor?
solution: Aurangzeb imprisoned his father Shahjahan and gained power by killing his brothers. He assumed the title of 'Alamgir', which means 'World Conqueror'.

question: Why did Shahjahan build 'Machhli Bhawan' in 'Agra Fort'?
options: There were other parts of the fort for prisoners.
There were fountains and beautiful gardens for entertainment and seating for the court ladies.
solution: Machli Bhavan was famous for its beauty and peace. Shahjahan used to sit here and have informal discussions with his courtiers.

question: During the invasion of 'Nadir Shah', which Mughal minister betrayed him and invited him to come to Delhi?
solution: Saadat Khan was the Nawab of Awadh. He instigated Nadir Shah that if he looted Delhi, he would get treasure worth crores. Later, fearing the torture of Nadir Shah, he committed suicide.

question: Sher Shah Suri had fixed the rate of 'land revenue' as what part of the production?
solution: Sher Shah had created three categories of land (good, medium, bad) for tax assessment and determined the rent by taking their average. This rule was applicable everywhere except fertile areas like Multan.

question: What was the name of Shahjahan's eldest son who translated the Upanishads into Persian?
solution: Shahjahan wanted to make Dara Shikoh his successor, but Aurangzeb defeated him in the war of succession and killed him. Due to Dara's generosity he is also called 'Laghu Akbar'.

question: What was the main function of 'Mir-i-Atish' in the Mughal administration?
options: The head of the royal kitchen was looked after by 'Mir-e-Samaan'.
solution: Their artillery played a big role in the success of the Mughals. Mir-e-Aatish ensured that the cannons were always ready and used at the right place during the war.

question: Which Mughal emperor is famous for establishing the 'Chain of Justice' (Zanjeer-e-Adal)?
solution: There were 60 bells attached to this chain and when it was pulled, the emperor would get immediate information. This reflects Jahangir's just image towards his subjects.

question: In which language was Babar's autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Babri' originally written?
solution: In Tuzuk-e-Babri, Babar has described the natural beauty, fruits and animals and birds of India. Madam Beveridge translated it into English.

question: At which place did Jahangir install his Chain of Justice?
solution: The Chain of Justice was made of pure gold and had 60 bells. Any aggrieved person could pull this chain and seek justice directly from the emperor.

question: On what is the architecture of 'Panch Mahal' located in Fatehpur Sikri based?
solution: Panch Mahal is also called 'Hawa Mahal' because it is completely open and rests on pillars. It was built for the entertainment of queens and court ladies.

question: Akbar, influenced by the debate on 'Ibadat Khana' in 'Fatehpur Sikri', gave the title of 'Jagatguru' to which Jain scholar?
solution: Akbar was greatly influenced by the philosophy of different religions. He studied not only from Islam but also from scholars of Hinduism, Jainism, Zoroastrianism and Christianity.

question: In which special formation did Babar arrange his army in the battle of Panipat?
solution: The Tulughma formation consisted of 'Haravaal' (advance group), 'Jaranghar' (left wing) and 'Baranghar' (right wing). This method led Babur to victory despite having less soldiers.

question: Which new practice did Akbar introduce for relations with 'Rajputs' which was called 'Sulh-i-Kul'?
options: Keeping the Rajputs out of his capital
solution: It was only because of the policy of Sulh-e-Kul that Akbar could become a national emperor. He felt that cooperation and religious peace of the majority of the population were essential for a stable empire.

question: In which year did Babar assume the title of 'Padshah'?
solution: Babur took the title of Padshah to show his position as independent and sovereign. Before this, Mughal ancestors used to call themselves Mirza. This shows his political maturity and ambition to expand his empire.

question: By which method did Babar confuse Ibrahim Lodhi's army in the battle of 'Panipat'?
options: The echo of cannons and the elephants going crazy
solution: Lodhi's army was huge but unorganized. Babur had only 12,000 soldiers, but his artillery and military discipline defeated an army of 1 lakh.

question: Which British officer shot the two sons of the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar at the 'Khooni Darwaza' of Delhi?
solution: Khooni Darwaza is one of the historical gates of Delhi. This cruelty of Hudson gave the message of completely crushing the rebellion. Jafar did not lose patience even after seeing the severed heads of his sons.

question: In which year was 'Ibadat Khana' located in Fatehpur Sikri opened for all religions?
solution: The debates taking place in the Ibadat Khana made Akbar realize that truth is not the inheritance of any one religion. This helped him to develop universal tolerance towards all religions.

question: From whose time did Sher Shah Suri re-adopt the practice of 'Dagging the horses' (Dag-huliya) under 'administrative reforms'?
solution: The Daagh system ensured that the Mansabdars did not bring horses of poor breed during times of war. The Hulia system ensured the identity of the soldiers.

question: 'Birbal' died while suppressing which rebellion in Akbar's court?
solution: Birbal's death was a great personal blow to Akbar. It is said that Akbar remained in mourning for several days and had stopped eating and drinking. Birbal was his dearest friend among his Navratnas.

question: Where did Akbar establish 'Ibadat Khana' for religious discussions?
solution: Initially only Muslim scholars came to Ibadat Khana, but later Akbar opened it to Hindu, Jain, Christian and Parsi scholars also. From here Akbar's policy of religious tolerance developed.

question: Which place was chosen by Shahjahan for 'Jharokha Darshan' in 'Agra Fort'?
solution: Jharokha Darshan was a popular tradition of the Mughals which was started by Akbar. Its objective was to establish direct contact between the king and the subjects.

question: Along with the construction of 'Sarais', which trees were ordered to be planted near them by Sher Shah Suri?
solution: Sher Shah made the trade routes very comfortable by planting trees on both sides of the roads. His foresight is still an inspiration for modern road construction.

question: While reintroducing 'Jizya' tax, Aurangzeb had announced to keep which class free from it, although later it was also included?
options: Initially no one was kept completely free, except the very poor
solution: Jizya tax was one of the most controversial policies of Aurangzeb. This created distrust among Hindus towards the Mughals and pitted many regional powers against the Mughals.

question: In which year did Akbar end 'Jizya' tax?
solution: The abolition of Jizya tax was an important part of Akbar's 'Sulh-i-Kul' policy. However, it was later re-imposed by the radical Aurangzeb in 1679.

question: Which Indian tradition has Jahangir praised in his autobiography in which 'justice' is considered paramount?
solution: Jahangir wanted to see himself as an ideal just ruler. He had said that in matters of justice he would not take sides even against his princes or wives.

question: What was the main function of 'Mutasaddi' in the Mughal administration?
options: Administering ports and managing maritime trade
It was the job of Mir-e-Samaan to supply supplies to the army.
It was the duty of Mir-i-Tuzuk to welcome foreign messengers.
solution: Surat was the largest and most prosperous port of the Mughals. Mutsaddee kept track of the customs duty received from there and looked after the facilities of Haj pilgrims.

question: Who was the ruler of 'Malwa' who rebelled against the Mughals during the reign of Humayun?
solution: Baz Bahadur was a great musician but he was not a skilled commander. During the time of Humayun he maintained his independence, but later Akbar defeated him and took him into Mughal service.

question: What did Akbar build in Fatehpur Sikri to commemorate the victory of Gujarat?
solution: Buland Darwaza is made of red and yellow sandstone. It was added as the southern entrance of Jama Masjid. Its grandeur reflects Akbar's military power and interest in architecture.

question: In which year did Shahjahan shift his capital from Agra to Delhi?
solution: The purpose of making Delhi the capital was to make the administration of the empire more centralized and to provide a new grandeur. Shahjahanabad was famous for its beauty.

question: On the request of which Mughal princess did Aurangzeb expel the musicians from the court?
options: This was his own decision, not a request from any princess
solution: Aurangzeb had removed music from the court considering it against Islam. When the musicians held a 'musical funeral' in protest, Aurangzeb ordered "Bury it so deep that its sound may never be heard again."

question: Which new style was introduced in 'painting' during the period of Jahangir in which a 'halo' was created around the human face?
solution: Jahangir wanted to show himself as a king with divine light. In his paintings he is often shown with angels and a halo.

question: Which famous market of Delhi was completely burnt during the invasion of 'Nadir Shah'?
solution: The destruction of Chandni Chowk became a symbol of the decline of Mughal economic power. It took decades for Delhi to recover after the plunder of Nadir Shah.

question: In which year did Shahjahan shift his capital from Agra to Delhi?
solution: The Red Fort and Jama Masjid of Delhi are excellent examples of Shahjahan's architecture. 'Diwan-i-Aam' and 'Diwan-i-Khas' are located inside the Red Fort.

question: In which language did Babar write his autobiography 'Tuzuk-e-Babri'?
solution: Babar's autobiography is counted among the best works of world literature. In this he has given a very vivid description of India's nature, animals and birds and the political scenario of that time.

question: Where was the city of 'Din-Panaah' established during the reign of Humayun?
solution: Humayun died due to falling from the stairs of the library (Sher Mandal) of this humble refuge. Historians have said about Humayun that "he stammered throughout his life and died stammering."

question: At which place did the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar die?
solution: It is written on the tomb of Bahadur Shah Zafar that "Zafar was so unfortunate that he did not get even two yards of land to be buried in his motherland." He became a symbol of the tragic end of the Mughal dynasty.

question: 'Baburnama' was translated into Persian by 'Abdul Rahim Khan-e-Khana' during the reign of which Mughal ruler?
solution: The Persian translation of the Baburnama was a means for the Mughals to understand their roots. Abdul Rahim Khan-e-Khana was the son of Bairam Khan and was also a great scholar and poet.

question: During whose period was the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) fought?
solution: The Third Battle of Panipat decided that the Marathas would not rule over India, paving the way for the British to conquer India. Shah Alam II was the Mughal emperor at that time.

question: Who built the 'Peacock Throne' (Takht-i-Taus)?
solution: The Peacock Throne was looted and taken away by the Iranian invader Nadir Shah in 1739. After this it could never return to India.

question: What was the childhood name of Shahjahan?
solution: The reign of Shahjahan is considered the 'Golden Age' of Mughal architecture. He built not only the Taj Mahal but also the Red Fort and Jama Masjid of Delhi.

question: The illustration of which famous manuscript in the field of 'painting' started during the reign of Humayun?
solution: Humayun started the illustration of Hamzanama and Akbar got it completed. A wonderful confluence of Iranian and Indian styles can be seen in it.

question: What special rule did Akbar make to discourage the practice of 'Sati'?
options: Made it mandatory only for Brahmins
Government permission and investigation was mandatory before sati could be performed.
Gave death penalty to those who took part in it
solution: Akbar took many steps for women's rights. He encouraged widow remarriage and also fixed the marriageable age of girls and boys to prevent child marriage.

question: In which city did Babar construct 'Aaram Bagh'?
solution: Babar was very fond of gardens. He built Aaram Bagh in Agra. After his death, he was first buried here, later he was taken to Kabul as per his wish.

question: What did 'Nadir Shah' ask from the Mughal emperor to stop the massacre in Delhi?
options: Begging for his life and immense wealth
solution: Nadir Shah collected money from every house of Delhi. His soldiers looted so much that the prosperity of Delhi ended forever.

question: For what purpose did Akbar get 'Diwan-i-Khas' constructed in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
options: There were separate grounds for watching the elephant fight.
solution: There is a carved pillar in the middle of Diwan-i-Khas whose roof is connected to four paths. This reflects Akbar's policy of listening to all ideologies and being at the center of them.

question: What was the main reason for Babar's victory in the first battle of Panipat?
options: Tulughma war policy and use of gunpowder
solution: On 21 April 1526, Babar defeated Ibrahim Lodhi in the field of Panipat. In this war, Babar used the Tulughma method learned from the Uzbegs, in which the army was divided into centre, right and left wings and surrounded the enemy.

question: Who built Humayun's Tomb (Delhi)?
solution: Humayun's Tomb is the first example of 'Charbagh' style in India. It is considered the precursor of the Taj Mahal because Shahjahan was inspired by its architecture.

question: What did Sher Shah Suri change the name of 'Pataliputra' which is the capital of Bihar in modern times?
solution: Sher Shah built a fort at the confluence of Ganga and Son rivers. The geographical location of Patna was very important from trade and military point of view, which Sher Shah understood very well.

question: Where did Humayun establish the city of 'Din-Panah'?
solution: Deen-panah was called 'shelter of religion'. Sher Shah Suri later destroyed it and built 'Purana Qila' there. Only the 'Sher Mandal' (library) of Humayun's city now remains as a relic.

question: Despite Aurangzeb banning music, which instrument was himself proficient in playing?
solution: Aurangzeb had expelled singers from the court, after which music flourished in regional capitals and among the general public. During his period many important texts on music were written in Persian.

question: Which officer was appointed by Sher Shah Suri for the management of 'Sarais'?
solution: The network of inns was Sher Shah's greatest achievement. This greatly increased the exchange of information and mobility of troops within the empire.

question: Which new city was established by Shahjahan by shifting his capital from Agra to Delhi?
solution: Shahjahanabad was famous for its wide roads, Jama Masjid and Red Fort. This made Delhi the permanent center of the Mughals which remained till 1857.

question: In which river did Humayun jump to save his life after the 'Battle of Kannauj' (1540)?
solution: Humayun made Bhishti, who saved his life, half-day king, and issued leather coins in his memory. This reflects both the generosity of Humayun and the instability of his rule.

question: Which Sikh Guru was hanged during the reign of Jahangir?
solution: Guru Arjun Dev was accused of blessing Khusro and providing financial assistance. This was the first major incident of the Mughal-Sikh conflict that led the peaceful Sikh community towards militarization.

question: Which huge gate was built by Akbar to commemorate the victory of Gujarat?
solution: Akbar conquered Gujarat in 1573. Buland Darwaza is made of red and yellow sandstone. It is built as the southern entrance of Jama Masjid of Fatehpur Sikri.

question: Who translated 'Tuzuk-e-Babri' into Persian as 'Baburnama'?
solution: It became popular in the Mughal court only after Baburnama was translated into Persian. Later European scholars made its English translations based on this Persian version.

question: Who was the one among Akbar's 'Navratnas' who translated 'Baburnama' from Turkish language into Persian?
solution: Rahim not only translated but he also left his deep mark in Hindi literature through 'Rahim's Couplets'. He was also one of Akbar's most trusted generals.

question: What was the main function of 'Mir Bakshi' in the Mughal administration?
options: In charge of the royal kitchen
Head of the military department and keeping records of the Mansabdars
solution: Mir Bakshi was the backbone of the Mansabdari system. He supervised the arrangements for keeping the soldiers in good order and branding the horses. After the emperor, his advice in military matters was considered the most important.

question: What was the post of 'Mir-i-Barr' during the Mughal period?
options: In charge of the royal forests and hunting grounds
In charge of the royal cook
solution: Forests were the main source of wood and elephants for the Mughals. The Mir-i-Bar ensured that the royal hunting grounds remained safe and hunting could be done there only by the Emperor or with his permission.

question: Which principle was applied by Sher Shah Suri for 'Crime Control'?
options: Only the principle of death penalty
solution: Due to this strict policy the crime rate became minimum during the time of Sher Shah. There was so much fear of the law among the people that incidents of theft had almost ended. This was the biggest success of his police system.

question: With which stone did Akbar construct 'Buland Darwaza' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
solution: Buland Darwaza is not only a victory monument, but it is also a symbol of the grandeur of Mughal architecture. Its height and its carvings make it one of the great monuments of the world.

question: What was the head of 'Suba' (province) called in the Mughal Empire?
solution: Akbar had divided his empire into 12 provinces, the number of which later increased to 15 and during the time of Aurangzeb it reached 21. Every province had the same administrative system as the centre.

question: What was the post of 'Mir-i-Atish' in the Mughal administration?
options: The head of the royal stable was called 'Akhur-Beg'.
solution: A major secret of the Mughals' success was their powerful artillery. Mir-e-Aatish used to ensure that the cannons and gunpowder were in perfect condition during the war.

question: When did Akbar shift his capital from Fatehpur Sikri to Lahore?
solution: Akbar made Lahore his main center in the last years of his reign to secure the borders of the empire.

question: Where was 'Bibi Ka Maqbara' which is considered a copy of Taj Mahal built by Aurangzeb?
solution: Bibi Ka Maqbara is also called the 'Crown of the Deccan'. It is similar to the Taj Mahal in size but the use of marble is less and the grandeur of the architecture is also not the same.

question: Which Maratha prince was freed from Mughal captivity by 'Bahadur Shah I' after the death of Aurangzeb?
solution: The purpose of freeing Sahu ji was to create internal discord among the Marathas (between Tarabai and Sahu) so that the Mughals could establish peace in South India. This policy was successful to some extent.

question: What color palace had Shahjahan planned for his Begum Mumtaz Mahal for her tomb in front of 'Taj Mahal'?
solution: Many historians consider the story of the 'Black Taj Mahal' to be a mere fiction as the black ruins found across the Yamuna were actually pieces of white marble blackened with time. Ultimately Aurangzeb buried Shahjahan next to Mumtaz.

question: What was the name of the 'pond' that Akbar built near the 'Dargah of Salim Chishti' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
solution: There is a stage in the middle of Anoop Talab where concerts were held while sitting. This pond is located very near Akbar's palace (Khwabgah).

question: At which place did the war of succession take place between the sons of Shahjahan in which Aurangzeb was victorious?
solution: Aurangzeb gained power by defeating all his brothers (Dara, Shuja and Murad). He also imprisoned his father Shahjahan in Agra Fort where he died.

question: Where is Akbar's tomb located?
solution: The construction work of Akbar's tomb was completed by his son Jahangir. The specialty of this building is that it lacks a dome and is a pyramidal multi-storey structure.

question: Why did Aurangzeb stop inscribing 'Kalma' on coins?
options: So that the Kalma does not become impure due to coins coming under his feet
The metal of the coins was decreasing
He did not like the Arabic script.
solution: Aurangzeb stopped many practices which he considered un-Islamic. He also banned the celebration of the Parsi New Year 'Nauroz'.

question: Akbar abolished Jizya tax and adopted the policy of 'Sulh-e-Kul', what is its literal meaning?
solution: Due to the policy of Sulh-e-Kul, Akbar is counted among the greatest emperors of India. He felt that the cooperation of the majority of Hindus was essential for a stable empire.

question: Which painter was sent by Jahangir as a messenger to paint the portrait of the Shah of Persia (Iran)?
solution: Bishan Das, while living in Iran, made such vivid pictures of the Shah and his family that Jahangir was very pleased with them and gifted him an elephant and precious gems.

question: Sher Shah Suri had fixed the tax rate as what part of the production?
solution: Sher Shah introduced systems like 'Patta' (title deeds) and 'Qabuliyat' (contract letters) which established a direct relationship between the farmer and the state and reduced the exploitation of middlemen.

question: What was the security called for carrying the revenue collected by 'Aamli' to the center in the Mughal administration?
solution: The communication and transportation system of the Mughals was very strong. Reaching a secure center of revenue was essential to the stability of the empire.

question: What was Jahangir's childhood name?
solution: Jahangir ascended the throne in 1605 under the name of 'Noor-ud-din Mohammad Salim'. He is remembered for establishing the Chain of Justice (Zanjeer-e-Adal).

question: At which place did Jahangir install the chain of justice in 'Agra Fort'?
options: From the banks of river Yamuna straight to the 'Shah Burj' of the fort
solution: There were 60 bells attached to this chain. Any victim could pull it out at any time, letting the emperor know immediately that someone needed justice. This was the biggest symbol of Jahangir's justice.

question: Which soldiers came under 'Mir-e-Aatish' in the Mughal administration?
options: Naval officers were under the command of 'Mir-e-Bahar'.
All the employees of the artillery department and the soldiers using heavy guns were under it.
solution: The importance of artillery was decisive in the war victories of the Mughals. Mir-e-Aatish used to ensure that the cannons were deployed at the right place during the siege of forts.

question: The concept of 'Watan Jagir' was related to which community?
solution: Akbar made matrimonial and friendly relations with the Rajputs and made them a part of the Mughal system. Due to Watan Jagir, Rajputs served the Mughals for a long time.

question: During whose reign did the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) take place?
solution: Shah Alam II spent most of his time outside Delhi as he was on the run from the fear of his ministers. Later he became a pensioner of the British. The battle of Buxar (1764) was fought during his period.

question: Which fifth Guru of the Sikhs was given death sentence by Jahangir for helping the rebel prince Khusro?
solution: Jahangir had accused Guru Arjun Dev of treason. After this incident, relations between the Sikhs and the Mughals became bitter forever and the Sikhs took steps towards militarization.

question: Which commander of 'Ahmednagar' did Jahangir send his son Khurram to defeat?
solution: It was only after this success of Khurram that Jahangir gave him the title of 'Shahjahan'. Malik Ambar had stopped the expansion of the Mughals in South India for a long time.

question: What was the arrangement for cooking food for Hindus in the 'Sarais' established by Sher Shah Suri?
options: They had to cook their own food
There were no special arrangements for them
solution: The inns had fodder for horses, bedding for travelers and strong security arrangements. These sarais played an important role in 'nation building' by connecting different parts of the empire.

question: From where did Babur mainly recruit 'archers' in his army?
solution: The archers in Babar's cavalry were very powerful. He was adept at shooting arrows by turning back from a running horse (Parthian Shot). This technique confused Ibrahim Lodhi's huge army.

question: What was the function of 'Daroga-e-Farashkhana' in the Mughal administration?
options: Managing the imperial tents, carpets, and furnishings
solution: When the Mughal emperor was on a trip, the Farashkhana department ensured that the emperor's luxurious tent was set up everywhere on time.

question: Aurangzeb is buried in 'Khuldabad', this place is near which modern city?
solution: There is no grand dome or building on the tomb of Aurangzeb. It is an open tomb which reflects his religious simplicity. Nearby is the Dargah of Sufi saint Zainuddin Shirazi.

question: What has historian Lane-Poole said about Humayun?
options: He staggered throughout his life and died while stammering
He was the greatest conqueror of the Mughals
solution: Humayun died in 1556 after falling from the stairs of the 'Din-Panah' library in Delhi. His generosity often became his political weakness.

question: At which place during Humayun's reign did 'Kamram Mirza' harass him the most?
solution: The betrayal of Humayun's brothers is a sad story of Mughal history. Humayun forgave him again and again, but he repeatedly weakened the power of the Mughals in his greed for power.

question: Which Mughal Vizier tried to negotiate peace with Nadir Shah during his invasion?
solution: Nizam-ul-Mulk established the Hyderabad state. He was the most experienced politician of the Mughal court, but due to factionalism in the court he could not save the empire from Nadir Shah.

question: Why did Akbar build 'Diwan-i-Khas' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
options: To hear the complaints of the general public, 'Diwan-i-Aam' was used.
For the accommodation of foreign ambassadors, there were separate inns and guest rooms for the ambassadors.
solution: At the center of the Diwan-i-Khas is a carved pillar with four niches connected to its roof. It was the center of Akbar's administrative skills and his deep discussions.

question: For how many days did 'Nadir Shah' order the massacre in Delhi?
options: About 1 day (there was an order of a few hours which lasted the whole day)
solution: Nadir Shah's soldiers had turned the streets of Delhi red with blood. It is said that about 30,000 people were killed. Nadir Shah stopped the massacre only after Mohammad Shah Rangeela cried and pleaded.

question: Who started the practice of 'Du-aspa' and 'Sih-aspa' during the reign of Jahangir?
solution: Do-aspa meant that the soldier would have two horses, and sih-aspa meant three horses. This increased the army's mobility and combat capability, as tired horses could be replaced quickly.

question: Which Iranian Shah helped Humayun to regain the throne of Delhi?
solution: Iranian help gave Humayun the strength to fight against his brothers and the Afghans. With this help Humayun conquered Kabul and Kandahar and finally returned to India in 1555.

question: From where did 'Nadir Shah' get the 'Kohinoor Diamond' while returning from Delhi?
options: Stolen directly from the royal treasury
From the turban of the Mughal emperor Mohammad Shah
He had also taken away the Peacock Throne in which the Kohinoor was studded.
solution: The Kohinoor diamond was the pinnacle of the Mughals' glory. After Nadir Shah it went to Ahmed Shah Abdali and ultimately came into the hands of the British through Ranjite Singh.

question: Whom did Babar declare as his successor before his death?
solution: Following his father's will, Humayun divided the empire among his brothers, which later became the main reason for his downfall as the brothers challenged his authority.

question: Sher Shah Suri introduced the system of 'Patta' and 'Kabuliyat' for land revenue, what was the meaning of 'Kabuliyat'?
options: Land ownership certificate given by the government
Written acceptance of payment of revenue by the farmer
solution: The patta and kabuliyat system established a direct relationship between the farmers and the state. This reduced the influence of middlemen and provided protection to farmers from exploitation.

question: Which architect was appointed by Shahjahan to build the 'Red Fort' in his capital Delhi?
solution: The Red Fort is the pinnacle of Mughal architecture. It took about 10 years to build it. It is called 'Red Fort' because of the red color of its walls, which are made of red sandstone.

question: Which scholar among the 'Navratnas' in Akbar's court was the author of 'Akbarnama'?
solution: Abul Fazal not only wrote history but he also provided a philosophical basis to Akbar's policies. He was Akbar's closest ideological companion.

question: Which measurement was used by Sher Shah Suri for 'measuring land'?
solution: Sher Shah made the measurement of land very accurate. He maintained records of each village and ensured that rent was collected from farmers based on the fertility of their land.

question: Whose son was the famous poet of Akbar's court 'Abdul Rahim Khan-e-Khana'?
solution: Rahim was a great poet who wrote 'couplets' in Hindi. He was also a scholar of Persian, Turkish and Sanskrit. It was he who translated Tuzuk-e-Babri into Persian.

question: Who was the assistant of 'Muqaddam' in the Mughal administration who kept the accounts of the village?
solution: The pair of Muqaddam (headman) and Patwari ran the Mughal rural system smoothly for centuries. The success of the revenue system depended on these local officials.

question: How much wealth did 'Nadir Shah' loot from the Mughals while returning after the massacre in Delhi?
options: Approximately Rs 70 crores and the Peacock Throne
solution: After the invasion of Nadir Shah, the economic back of the Mughal Empire broke. He looted every rich and poor of Delhi. After his departure, the Mughal emperor had no money left even to pay salaries to his army.

question: Which building built by Akbar was inspired by the style of 'Buddh Vihar'?
solution: Panch Mahal is also called 'Hawa Mahal'. It is completely open air and was built for the entertainment of queens. It is a fine example of the coordination of Indian styles in Akbar's architecture.

question: After which war did Babur decide to stay in India even though his soldiers wanted to go back?
solution: Babur's soldiers did not like the heat and dust of India. Babur gave an impressive speech to motivate them and compared the poverty of Kabul with the prosperity of India, convincing the soldiers to stay.

question: Where was the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled after the rebellion of 1857?
solution: It is written on the tomb of Bahadur Shah Zafar that "Zafar was so unfortunate that he did not get even two yards of land to be buried in his motherland." With him the 300 year old Mughal rule in India came to an end.

question: What is the height of 'Buland Darwaza' which makes it the highest gateway in India?
solution: Buland Darwaza is the southern entrance of Jama Masjid of Fatehpur Sikri. The height of its stairs is also included in this. There is a Persian inscription on its main gate regarding Jesus Christ which gives the message of religious harmony.

question: What was the real name of Jahangir's wife Noorjahan?
solution: Nur Jahan was an extremely influential woman who played an active role in the governance of the state. She became 'Badshah Begum' and coins were also issued in her name.

question: What was the post of 'Mir-i-Tuzuk' in the Mughal administration?
options: The one who kept accounts of revenue was called 'Mustaufi'.
In charge of festivities and court etiquette
solution: The Mughal court was known for its strict protocols. Mir-i-Tuzuk ensured that each courtier stood according to his rank and greeted the emperor correctly.

question: Shahjahan built the Taj Mahal in the memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, her real name was Arjumand Bano Begum, which title was she given?
solution: Mumtaz Mahal was Shah Jahan's favorite wife and accompanied him on his military campaigns. He died at the birth of his 14th child.

question: What was the main function of 'Muhtasib' officers during the Mughal period?
options: Protecting public morality and enforcing Sharia law
solution: Aurangzeb had appointed Muhtasibs to ban liquor, gambling and music. He also removed the astrologers and singers in the court.

question: What was the real name of Sher Shah Suri?
solution: Farid Khan started his administrative career by taking over his father's estate. His administrative talent and military skills led him to the position of Sultan of Delhi.

question: What was the silver coin introduced by Sher Shah Suri called?
solution: Sher Shah Suri's economic reforms were extremely effective. He introduced a system of standard weights and measures and fixed a fixed exchange rate between the silver rupee and the price of copper.

question: Which Afghan ruler did Humayun defeat in the 'Battle of Sirhind' (1555) to regain his power?
solution: The victory of Sirhind ended the period of exile of the Mughals. Although Humayun lived only a year after this victory, it had set the stage for Akbar.

question: What was the real name of Sher Shah Suri?
solution: Sher Shah Suri founded the Second Afghan Empire. He defeated Humayun and captured Delhi and made many administrative reforms which later became a guide for Akbar.

question: In memory of which victory did Akbar start the construction of 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
options: This new city was planned by Akbar after the Chittor and Ranthambore conquests and campaigns of 1569–70.
solution: Fatehpur Sikri was the capital of the Mughals from 1571 to 1585. Due to lack of water, Akbar later had to leave it and go to Lahore. Jodha Bai Mahal, Birbal Mahal and Diwan-i-Khas are famous here.

question: What was the average basis of production taken by Sher Shah Suri to determine the 'category of land'?
options: Average of good, medium and bad land
solution: The main quality of Sher Shah's revenue system was its fairness. He gave the farmers the option to pay taxes in cash or in the form of grains.

question: In the Mughal period, 'Aamli' or 'Amal-Gujar' officer was related to which administrative level?
options: Revenue collection at the district (government) level
Keeping records at the village level
solution: The main function of Amal-gujar was to ensure that farmers paid taxes on time and that revenue was assessed correctly. He was responsible for implementing Todarmal's revenue system at the grassroots level.

question: Which Hindu state was described by Babar in his autobiography as the most powerful state of North India?
solution: It is written about Rana Sanga in Baburnama that "by his bravery he had attained the highest position among the Hindu kings." Defeating Sanga was the biggest challenge for Babar to establish his foothold in India.

question: Which stone was mainly used by Shahjahan for the construction of 'Jama Masjid' (Delhi)?
solution: Jama Masjid is one of the largest mosques in India. Its minarets and domes enhance its grandeur. It took about 6 years to make it.

question: Which Bengal ruler who helped Mahmud Lodhi was defeated by Babur in the 'Battle of Ghaghra' (1529)?
solution: After the victory of Ghaghra, Babar made a non-aggression pact with the Sultan of Bengal. With this the eastern border of the Mughals became secure.

question: In which year did Aurangzeb re-introduce 'Jizya' tax?
solution: The reintroduction of the Jizya tax caused great resentment among the Rajputs, Marathas and other Hindu communities, leading to intensified rebellions against the Mughal Empire.

question: Who built the 'Tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula' which is completely made of white marble?
solution: Itamad-ud-Daula's tomb is the first building in Mughal architecture in which 'pietra dura' (stone carving and inlaying of precious stones) was used extensively. It is considered the predecessor of the Taj Mahal.

question: Sher Shah Suri appointed which officer at the 'Pargana' level to assess the revenue for the collection of taxes?
solution: Sher Shah's administration was highly decentralized and well organized. He had set clear responsibilities for each post. Amil remained in direct contact with the farmers so that corruption could be reduced.

question: Why did Akbar build 'Turkish Sultana's Palace' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
options: It is called the 'Jewel of Stone' for one of its queens and because of the intricate carvings on its walls
There was a separate building for the kitchen.
solution: The Turkish Sultana's palace is small but its beauty is amazing. Its walls have carvings of birds, animals and flowers which are not found in any other palace of the Mughal period. Percy Brown has called it a 'pearl of architecture'.

question: What was the real name of 'Noorjahan'?
solution: Noor Jahan was one of the most powerful women in Mughal history. He formed the 'Nur Jahan faction' (junta) which included his father Itmad-ud-Daula, brother Asaf Khan and Prince Khurram. Coins were also issued in his name.

question: Why did Shahjahan build 'Musamman Burj' inside 'Agra Fort'?
options: For his wife and daughters to sit from where they can see the Taj Mahal
There were separate rooms for the safety of the treasure.
solution: Musamman Burj is famous for its intricate carvings and pietra dura work. Shahjahan spent the last eight years of his life looking at the Taj Mahal from here. It is also called 'Shah Burj'.

question: Which building built by Shahjahan is called 'Mirror of Polished Stones'?
solution: Sheesh Mahal was built for the bathing and rest of the royal family. When a candle was lit inside it, the entire palace would glow due to the thousands of mirrors.

question: Which Sikh Guru's son 'Guru Hargobind' was put under house arrest by Jahangir in Gwalior Fort?
solution: Guru Hargobind was kept in captivity for almost two years. Later he was released and 52 Hindu kings were also released along with him, which is celebrated as 'Bandi Chhod Diwas'.

question: What was the main function of 'Qazi-ul-Qujat' in the Mughal administration?
options: In charge of the royal cook
Being the head of the justice department
The head of the royal security was looked after by the 'Kotwal' or military officer.
solution: Qazi-ul-Qujat recommended the appointment of provincial and local Qazis. He mainly settled disputes according to civil and religious laws (Sharia).

question: Aurangzeb attacked 'Jodhpur' due to the succession dispute of which Rajput state?
solution: The Rathore Rajputs of Marwar fought against Aurangzeb for 30 years under the leadership of Durgadas Rathore. This war greatly weakened the military power of the Mughals.

question: What was the main responsibility of 'Mir Bakshi' in the Mughal administration?
options: The head of the royal cook was called 'Mir-e-Samaan'.
solution: The post of Mir Bakshi was extremely powerful as he kept the list of Mansabdars and checked their military strength. His advice was important to the emperor in military matters.

question: Who was the only Hindu courtier to accept 'Deen-e-Ilahi'?
solution: Deen-e-Ilahi was not an organized religion, rather it was a moral code of conduct. Akbar did not impose it on anyone, due to which, apart from Birbal, very few people became its members.

question: Which title did Aurangzeb hold which means 'World Conqueror'?
solution: Aurangzeb's reign lasted from 1658 to 1707. He is considered to be the last great Mughal ruler during whom the Mughal Empire reached the peak of its geographical extent.

question: Whose descendant is Babar considered to be from his paternal side?
solution: Babur was very proud of the Timurid heritage. He established the Mughal Empire in India, but he always dreamed of regaining his ancestral lands in Central Asia.

question: Who composed 'Akbarnama' and 'Ain-i-Akbari'?
solution: Akbarnama is divided into three parts. The third part is called 'Ain-i-Akbari' which contains a detailed description of Akbar's administration, army, revenue and geography of the empire.

question: What was the main function of 'Mir-i-Tuzuk' in the Mughal administration?
options: Managing the etiquette and ceremonies of the court
It was the job of the Qazi to administer justice.
solution: The Mughal court was known for its strict etiquette. Mir-i-Tuzuk ensured that each courtier stood at his designated place and greeted the emperor correctly.

question: To whom did Humayun hand over the fort of 'Kandahar' after conquering it, as he had promised earlier?
options: He had given this promise to the Safavid ruler of Persia in return for the help of Shah Tahmasp.
Humayun won the fort only by defeating his brother Kamran.
solution: Although Humayun gave Kandahar to the Safavids, he later reconquered it. Kandahar was always a center of dispute between the Mughals and Persia as it was located on a strategic trade route.

question: Which Indian fruit has been described by Babar as the 'king of fruits' and the best in his autobiography?
solution: Baburnama is not just a political history, it is also a natural and cultural encyclopedia of 16th century India. He had made very detailed observations of the flora and fauna here.

question: In which king's palace was Akbar born in 1542?
solution: Akbar's mother's name was Hamida Banu Begum. Akbar had a troubled childhood and never received a formal education, yet he became a patron of great scholars and a very wise ruler.

question: With which state did Akbar first establish matrimonial relations under the 'Rajput Policy'?
solution: This treaty with Amer gave Akbar great generals like Man Singh, who won for the Mughals from Kabul to Bengal.

question: For what was the word 'Bakhshi' used during the Mughal period?
options: For tax collectors, they were called 'Karori' or 'Amal-Gujar'.
solution: Mir Bakshi was the highest military officer of the empire. Without his signature no soldier or mansabdar could receive salary.

question: For how many years did Babur live like a nomad after losing 'Fargana'?
options: For about 10 years between 1494 and 1504, Babar had to struggle a lot for his throne.
solution: This difficult time of Babar made him a strong and patient warrior. He wrote in his autobiography that "Adversities refine a man."

question: Which Hindu state was described by Babar in 'Baburnama' as the most powerful state of South India?
solution: Baburnama shows that Babur studied the political situation of the entire subcontinent, not just North India. He considered Krishnadev Rai as an ideal ruler.

question: Which hilly region did Aurangzeb make his main center for wars against the Sikhs?
solution: Guru Gobind Singh established the Khalsa Panth in Anandpur Sahib. The Mughals laid siege to this fort several times to suppress the growing power of the Sikhs, but Guru Gobind Singh did not give up.

question: During the reign of Humayun, Sher Shah Suri increased his power by capturing which important fort?
solution: The capture of Chunar fort gave Sher Shah access to the resources of Bihar and Bengal. Humayun's taking Sher Shah lightly proved to be his biggest mistake.

question: Which Mughal emperor gave the title of 'Raja' to 'Raja' Ram Mohan Roy?
solution: During the reign of Akbar II (1806-1837), the Mughal Empire was reduced to only the Red Fort and its power was completely lost.

question: 'Daroga-e-Dak Chowki' was the head of which department in the Mughal administration?
solution: Daroga-e-Dak post was considered the eyes and ears of the emperor. He collected information from every corner of the empire and gave it to the emperor every day.

question: Why did Akbar build 'Panch Mahal' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
options: To keep the treasure, there was a separate building called 'Treasury'.
For offering Namaz, Jama Masjid was there.
solution: The architecture of Panch Mahal is considered to be inspired by Buddhist monasteries. It has a total of 176 pillars. This building becomes smaller towards the top, which makes it very attractive.

question: Which famous garden was built by Jahangir in 'Srinagar'?
solution: Jahangir had a deep love for nature. He called Kashmir 'heaven on earth'. Shalimar Bagh is an excellent example of a terraced garden where water fountains and fountains add to its beauty.

question: The reign of which Mughal ruler is called the 'Golden Age' of the Mughal Empire?
solution: Shahjahan built magnificent buildings like Red Fort of Delhi, Jama Masjid, Taj Mahal of Agra and Moti Masjid (Agra). He popularized the 'Pietra Dura' style.

question: Where was Humayun born?
solution: Humayun means 'fortunate', but he is counted among the most unlucky Mughal emperors in history as he had to spend half his life in exile.

question: After the death of 'Birbal' in Akbar's court, which wise courtier was considered the chief advisor in his place?
solution: Like Birbal, the personality of Mulla Do Pyaza is also very famous in folklore. He was among Akbar's Navratnas and was a leader in intellectual discussions with the emperor.

question: After which war did Babar distribute silver coins as a gift to his subjects, due to which he was called 'Qalandar'?
solution: Qalandar means 'generous' or 'cheerful'. This excessive generosity of Babur had a bad impact on his treasury, but he created his image as a charitable ruler in Central Asia.

question: Babar's mother belonged to which famous Mongol dynasty?
solution: The name Mughals actually derives from the word Mongol. Babur was very proud of his mixed heritage, which made him known as a powerful warrior in Central Asia.

question: What did Sher Shah Suri change the name of 'Pataliputra'?
solution: Sher Shah built a huge fort at the confluence of Ganga and Son rivers. Patna later remained important for the Mughals from trade and strategic point of view.

question: Along with giving high positions to 'Rajputs', which special rights did Akbar give them?
options: Right to mint one's own coin
Right to keep foreign policy independent
Autonomous rule in their ancestral territory (Watan Jagir)
Right to marry a Mughal princess
solution: The policy of 'Watan Jagir' was the most successful diplomacy of Akbar. This also maintained the respect of the Rajputs and the Mughals also got their loyal soldiers.

question: Who was the last emperor of the Mughal Empire?
solution: Bahadur Shah Zafar was a famous Urdu poet. The British imprisoned him and sent him to jail in Myanmar where he died in 1862.

question: Which fruit of India has Babar praised the most in his autobiography?
solution: He has written in Baburnama that "Mango is that fruit in front of which all fruits pale in comparison." Babar was so fond of gardening that he gave instructions to develop new varieties of fruits in India.

question: In which year did Babur conquer Kabul?
solution: The conquest of Kabul was a major turning point in Babur's life. From here he heard about the wealth of India and started planning to attack India from the north-west.

question: Who was the chief architect of Taj Mahal?
solution: The construction of Taj Mahal started in 1632 and it took about 22 years to build. It is made of white Makrana marble and is one of the finest examples of the 'Pietra Dura' style.

question: Which Rajput ruler was defeated by Babur in the battle of Chanderi in 1528?
solution: After the conquest of Chanderi, Babar established his influence over the regions of Malwa and Bundelkhand. Rajputs had committed 'Jauhar' in this war also.

question: Which Iranian painter taught painting to Humayun during his exile and later came to India?
options: Mir Syed Ali and Abdul Samad
solution: Humayun was very fond of painting. He kept these artists with him even during the difficult times of exile. It was he who started the illustration of 'Dastan-e-Amir Hamza' (Hamzanama), which was the first major work of Mughal art.

question: In which year did Shahjahan become the Mughal emperor?
solution: The reign of Shahjahan is considered the 'Golden Age' of Mughal architecture. He built many grand monuments in Agra and Delhi which are still the pride of India.

question: In which famous battle (1671) did the Ahom commander 'Lachit Borphukan' defeat the Mughals?
solution: Lachit Borphukan, with his skillful strategy and bravery, forced Aurangzeb's huge army to retreat. In his memory the 'Lachit Borphukan Gold Medal' is awarded to the best cadet of the National Defense Academy (NDA).

question: The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar and whom?
solution: Bairam Khan led the Mughal army in this war. Hemu was close to victory but he became unconscious after an arrow hit his eye and the Mughal army turned the tables. This victory ensured the return of the Mughal Empire to India.

question: After which war did Babar assume the title of 'Ghazi'?
solution: The battle of Khanwa took place in 1527 between Babar and Rana Sanga of Mewar. Babar had declared this war as 'Jihad' and after the victory he assumed the title of Ghazi.

question: What was the 'Dahshala' system related to during the reign of Akbar?
solution: The Dahashala system saved farmers from uncertainty because they knew how much tax they had to pay. It also made the state's income stable and predictable.

question: What was the main function of 'Mir-e-Samaan' in the Mughal administration?
options: Management of the Imperial Household and Factories
solution: Mir-e-Sama was a very close officer of the emperor. He ensured the supply of all necessary items to the royal harem, festivals and during the emperor's visits.

question: What was the main function of 'Mir-i-Bahr' in the Mughal administration?
options: Believing the sea to be God
solution: Mir-e-Bahar was mainly active in the coastal provinces like Bengal and Gujarat. He attempted to build royal ships and stop piracy.

question: At which place during Humayun's reign did 'Askari' try to declare himself an independent ruler?
solution: The ambition of Humayun's brothers was his biggest enemy. He forgave them, but they betrayed them again and again.

question: Why did 'Queen Karnavati' send Rakhi to Humayun during his reign?
options: To protect Mewar from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat, the queen had sought help from Humayun considering him as her brother.
solution: Humayun accepted Rakhi but he stayed in Gwalior and could not reach Chittor on time. Due to this delay, Queen Karnavati had to commit Jauhar, which later saddened Humayun.

question: For which type of meetings did Akbar construct 'Diwan-i-Aam' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
options: To listen to the complaints of the common people and for public functions, here the emperor used to sit on a high platform and the public used to stand in the ground below.
There was a separate department for the inspection of treasury.
There were separate palaces for royal dances.
There was Diwan-i-Khas only for meeting with ministers.
solution: The Diwan-i-Aam of Fatehpur Sikri is a huge courtyard with verandahs built around it. This shows that Akbar wanted to be accessible to his subjects. From here he also used to inspect the royal elephants and horses.

question: Which city did Jahangir try to establish in the name of his wife Noorjahan but which could not succeed?
solution: Jahangir's love for Nur Jahan was so deep that he gave her priority in administration as well as in naming and coinage. Stamps in the name of Noorjahan were also in circulation.

question: At which place did Aurangzeb imprison 'Maratha King Sambhaji' and get him murdered (1689)?
solution: The brutal murder of Sambhaji further enraged the Marathas against Aurangzeb. After this the Marathas started a nationwide war to protect 'Swaraj'.

question: Which rebellious son was forgiven by Jahangir at the end of his reign?
solution: Jahangir's last days were tragic due to succession conflicts. Nur Jahan was supporting Shahryar, while the army and most of the emirs were with Khurram. Ultimately it was Khurram who succeeded in the name of Shahjahan.

question: What was the main reason given by Aurangzeb for re-introduction of 'Jizya' tax?
options: Considered it a religious duty and the establishment of an Islamic state
solution: The reintroduction of Jizya tax destroyed the image of the Mughals which Akbar had created. This inspired the Hindus to revolt against the Mughals.

question: Who built 'Bibi Ka Maqbara' in Aurangabad?
solution: Bibi Ka Maqbara is called the 'Taj Mahal of the South'. Although it is not as architecturally grand as the Taj Mahal, it is still an important building of the Mughal period.

question: Which famous Madrasa was renovated by Sher Shah Suri in the field of 'Education'?
solution: Sher Shah was an educated ruler and he greatly respected scholars. He patronized many poets and historians in his court.

question: The post of 'Mir Bakshi' in the Mughal administration was related to?
options: The head of the royal factories was called 'Mir-e-Samaan'.
solution: Mir Bakshi kept the list of Mansabdars and supervised the arrangements for the appearance of soldiers and the branding of horses. He was a very powerful official of the empire.

question: Against whom did Raja Chhatrasal of Bundelkhand rebel and establish an independent state?
solution: Raja Chhatrasal had met Shivaji Maharaj and learned guerrilla warfare methods from him. Aurangzeb finally tried to compromise by giving him a mansab of Rs 4000.

question: Which mosque was built by Shahjahan for his personal prayers in 'Agra Fort'?
solution: Moti Masjid of Agra is famous for its purity and shine. The use of white marble in Shahjahan's architecture shows his religious and artistic superiority.

question: Which general rebelled to reduce the influence of 'Noorjahan' during the reign of Jahangir?
solution: Mahabat Khan's rebellion was the peak of the internal politics of the Mughal court. Many old courtiers were angry because of Noor Jahan's excessive power. Ultimately Mahabat Khan accepted to support Shahjahan.

question: What was the main function of 'Mir-i-Arz' in the Mughal administration?
options: Delivering petitions from the general public to the emperor
It was the job of the Diwan to calculate the revenue.
solution: Mughal emperors considered 'justice' as the basis of their power. Mir-e-Araj used to ensure that the complaint of any poor or oppressed person was not left out from reaching the emperor.

question: In which year did Aurangzeb order the demolition of 'Vishwanath Temple of Banaras' and 'Keshavrai Temple of Mathura'?
solution: There were religious as well as political reasons behind Aurangzeb's policy of demolishing temples, such as suppressing rebellions. However, this undermined the roots of his empire.

question: Sher Shah Suri minted a silver coin, what was its name?
solution: Sher Shah's currency system was very systematic. The weight of his silver rupee was 178 grains. He completely eliminated adulteration in coins, which gave a great boost to trade.

question: What was the real name of Shahjahan's wife Mumtaz Mahal?
solution: Mumtaz Mahal died in Burhanpur in 1631. In his memory, Shahjahan built the world famous Taj Mahal in Agra.

question: What was the department of 'Mir-e-Aatish' related to in the Mughal administration?
solution: The role of artillery was decisive in the war victory of the Mughals. Mir-e-Aatish ensured that the cannons reached the battlefield at the right time and there was no shortage of ammunition for them.

question: From which place did Shahjahan get white marble for the construction of 'Taj Mahal'?
solution: A big secret of the beauty of the Taj Mahal is the Makrana marble, which appears to change its color according to the light. Thousands of elephants and camels were used to carry it.

question: What did Aurangzeb do to the court singers and musicians after he banned 'Music'?
options: He was released from service by giving him pension or employed in other works.
solution: After this decision of Aurangzeb, the center of music shifted from Delhi to regional capitals like Lucknow, Hyderabad and Banaras, where new musical styles developed.

question: What was the name of Humayun's mother?
solution: Before his death, Babur had declared Humayun as his successor and taught him to be generous towards his brothers, which Humayun followed.

question: Under whose leadership did Shahjahan get 'Chandni Chowk' constructed in his capital Delhi?
solution: Chandni Chowk was one of the most beautiful markets in the world at that time. A canal flowed through it which was called 'Nahar-e-Bahisht', in which the reflection of the moon looked very beautiful.

question: What was the childhood name of Shahjahan?
solution: Shahjahan was born in Lahore in 1592. His mother was Jagat Gosain (Princess of Jodhpur). His reign is called the 'Golden Age' of Mughal architecture.

question: What was the main function of 'Aamli' or 'Amal-Gujar' during the Mughal period?
solution: Amal-gujar ensured that the collection of revenue was as per the rules laid down by Todarmal. He struck a balance between protecting the interests of farmers and increasing the income of the state.

question: For how many hours did the 'Battle of Karnal' (1739) last between Nadir Shah and the Mughals?
solution: The battle of Karnal is a symbol of Nadir Shah's superior strategy and the weakness of the Mughals. After this defeat, Mughal emperor Mohammad Shah had to surrender and Delhi was looted.

question: 'Sadak-e-Azam' which is now called Grand Trunk Road, ran from where to where?
solution: Sher Shah had built four major roads to facilitate trade and communication. An inn was built every two miles along these roads where there was free provision of food and accommodation for the travelers.

question: Sher Shah Suri died during which campaign?
solution: At the time of Sher Shah's death he was on the threshold of victory. After his death, his son Islam Shah became the ruler, but the Suri dynasty gradually weakened and was eventually regained by Humayun.

question: In which year did Akbar start a new religion called 'Deen-e-Ilahi'?
solution: The main objective of Din-i-Ilahi was to create a common platform that would reduce disputes between different communities of the empire. The only Hindu to accept this was Birbal. It almost ended with the death of Akbar.

question: Why were the people of 'Mirza' dynasty against the Mughals during Humayun's reign?
options: They considered themselves the rightful heirs of Babur
He was only interested in painting
They joined forces with the British
They wanted to convert to Hinduism
solution: The rebellion of the Mirzas disturbed Humayun again and again. Whenever Humayun fought with external enemies, these Mirzas would rebel from behind. Akbar finally suppressed them completely.

question: Babur issued coins of which metal during his rule in 'Kabul' which were called 'Shahrukhi'?
solution: Shahrukh coins were named after Taimur's son Shahrukh Mirza. Babur's currency system was a symbol of his Timurid heritage.

question: What contribution did Jahangir make to the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) of 'Amritsar'?
options: He did not make any special direct contribution, but there was conflict with the Sikhs
He laid the foundation of the temple
solution: The martyrdom of Guru Arjun Dev during the reign of Jahangir created a long wall between the Sikhs and the Mughals. After this the Sikhs started taking up arms for their protection.

question: In which year did 'Todar Mal' fully implement the 'Dahshala' revenue system in Akbar's court?
solution: The Dahashala system provided financial stability to the Mughal Empire. In this, tax was determined on the basis of measurement and fertility of the land, which prevented arbitrary collection.

question: Which climate of India has Babar made fun of in his autobiography and described it as 'dirty'?
options: He did not like the dust and heat of India at all.
solution: Babur came from the cool and clear climate of Central Asia. He found it quite challenging to live in the dusty plains of India. He wrote that "there are no good melons here, no good horses and no ice cold water."

question: During the rise of Maratha Empire, who was the first person Aurangzeb sent to suppress Shivaji?
solution: Shivaji's attack on Shaista Khan dealt a deep blow to the prestige of the Mughals. Shivaji entered the Lal Mahal of Pune and cut off Shaista Khan's fingers.

question: In which year did 'Kandahar' go out of the hands of the Mughals forever during the reign of Shahjahan?
solution: The loss of Kandahar was a major strategic defeat for the Mughal Empire as it was the sentinel of the north-west frontier. Shahjahan sent three major expeditions to get it back which were unsuccessful.

question: Who was the famous painter of Jahangir's court who was given the title of 'Nadir-ul-Asar'?
solution: Jahangir himself was a great connoisseur of painting. He said that by looking at any painting he could tell which artist had made it. 'Naturalism' developed in painting during his period.

question: Babur used gunpowder and artillery for the first time in India during the siege of which fort?
solution: It was Babur who introduced gunpowder widely in the Indian warfare system. One of the main pillars of his military success were his skilled gunners Ustad Ali and Mustafa. The Bajaur and Bhera operations helped him understand the weaknesses of the Indian security system.

question: Which method was adopted by Sher Shah Suri for determining land revenue?
solution: Sher Shah used 'Sikandari Gaj' for measuring land. He decided to take 1/3 of the produce as tax. The main objective of his revenue system was to protect farmers from exploitation by middlemen.

question: Which administrative post was given to 'Birbal' in Akbar's court?
options: Head of the Charity Department and Justice Advisor
There are such stories only about the cook
solution: Birbal was given the title of 'Raja' by Akbar. He was the most popular among the Navaratnas of Akbar. Stories of his justice and intelligence are heard even today in India.

question: What concession did Aurangzeb try to give to Hindus in return of 'Jizya' tax, which was not successful?
options: Exemption from tax on joining the army
solution: Aurangzeb's policies alienated him from the majority of the population of his own state. The return of Jizya became a major social reason for the decline of the Mughal Empire.

question: How many inns did Sher Shah Suri build on the banks of 'Sadak-e-Azam' (GT Road)?
solution: In each Sarai there were separate arrangements for food and water for Hindus and Muslims. These inns also served as postal posts, making communication much faster.

question: By whom was 'Humayunnama' composed?
solution: Humayunnama is an important source to understand the history of the Mughal period. It gives a detailed description of Humayun's struggles and family life.

question: Which ruler of India has been described by Babar as the most powerful king in his autobiography?
solution: The Baburnama mentions the prosperity of the Vijayanagara Empire in South India and the rule of Krishnadeva Raya. This shows that Babar was well aware of the political situation in India.

question: Which Indian ruler has Babar described as 'great and worthy' in his autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Babri'?
solution: Baburnama shows that Babur had very good knowledge about the regional powers of India. He was impressed by Krishnadev Rai's army and his popularity.

question: In which battle did Sher Shah Suri defeat Humayun and assume the title of 'Sher Shah'?
solution: In the battle of Chausa, Humayun saved his life by crossing the river with the help of a Bhishti. This victory of Sher Shah established his complete control over Bihar and Bengal and shook the foundation of the Mughals.

question: Who was the assistant officer of 'Amal-Gujar' who kept land records during the Mughal period?
solution: Kanungo was a hereditary officer and had deep knowledge of local land customs and measurement. He was an important link for the Revenue Department.

question: What was the main responsibility of 'Kotwal' during the Mughal period?
options: Maintaining law and order in cities
solution: Kotwal was given the responsibility of patrolling the city at night and keeping records of visitors. His post was very important because he was directly connected with the public.

question: Which Rajput king was sent by Aurangzeb to capture 'Shivaji'?
solution: Raja Jai ​​Singh was a clever diplomat. He persuaded Shivaji to come to the Mughal court, although Shivaji later escaped from Aurangzeb's captivity.

question: What was the original name of Tansen, the famous musician of Akbar's court?
solution: Tansen was one of the Navratnas of Akbar. Akbar had given him the title of 'Mian'. Tansen composed many new ragas like Miyan Ki Todi and Miyan Ki Malhar.

question: What was Babar's real name?
solution: Babar, the founder of the Mughal Empire, was a resident of Fargana in Central Asia. He was born in 1483. He was a descendant of Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side. He laid the foundation of the Mughal dynasty in India in 1526.

question: Who was the famous poet of Akbar's court who received the title of 'Malik-ush-Shuara' (King of Poets)?
solution: Faizi had got Mahabharata (Razmnama) and Lilavati translated into Persian. He was also the head of Akbar's translation department.

question: Where did Akbar establish 'Ibadat Khana' (prayer house)?
solution: Initially Ibadat Khana was only for Muslim scholars, but in 1578 Akbar opened it to all religions (Hindu, Jain, Parsi, Christian). It was from here that Akbar realized that elements of truth are present in all religions.

question: From where did Shahjahan get the stones for the construction of 'Taj Mahal'?
options: Some stones came from Kabul during Babar's time but Makrana was the main stone for Taj Mahal.
solution: One of the main reasons for the beauty of Taj Mahal is the marble of Makrana. Thousands of elephants and camels were used to carry it. The specialty of this stone is that it does not turn yellow with time (if there is no pollution).

question: The most magnificent example of 'Pietra Dura' (inlay of gems on marble) is found in which Mughal building?
solution: The pietra dura technique is thought to have originally been inspired by Italy. It gained great popularity during the reign of Shahjahan. In this, grooves were made in marble and precious stones like sapphire, emerald and coral were filled in them.

question: In which year did Jahangir ban the use of 'tobacco'?
solution: Jahangir himself was fond of many drugs, but he saw tobacco as a social evil. However, despite its ban, tobacco cultivation and use continued to increase in India.

question: At which place near 'Diwan-i-Aam' in 'Fatehpur Sikri' did Akbar ban the sacrifice of animals?
options: In the Dargah of Salim Chishti
solution: Akbar gradually started leaning towards vegetarianism. He declared several days of the year as 'Prohibition Days' when slaughter houses remained closed.

question: Which Afghan ruler defeated Humayun in the battles of Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540)?
solution: Humayun's reign was divided into two parts. After being defeated in the battle of Kannauj (Bilgram) in 1540, he took refuge in the Safavid dynasty (Iran) and spent 15 years in exile.

question: In which year did Akbar abolish 'Pilgrimage Tax'?
solution: Abolition of pilgrimage tax was the initial phase of Akbar's liberal religious policy. He felt that it was unjust to tax a person for his faith. This increased the popularity of Akbar among the Hindu people.

question: Who composed 'Humayunnama', the biography of Humayun?
solution: Gulbadan Begum wrote this book on the request of Akbar. It contains interesting information about the struggles of Humayun's reign as well as the Mughal harem and family life.

question: Which invader looted the famous 'Peacock Throne' (Takht-i-Taus)?
solution: The Peacock Throne was a symbol of the luxury of Shahjahan and the splendor of the Mughals. It was studded with immense gold and precious gems. After his departure the shine of Mughal power faded.

question: Which famous waterfall or Chashma was developed by Jahangir near 'Srinagar'?
solution: Jahangir was so fond of gardening and water sources that he built many springs and canals in Kashmir. He believed that the sound of flowing water gives peace to the soul.

question: To which English traveler did Jahangir give the title of 'English Khan'?
solution: William Hawkins reached Surat in 1608 in a ship named Hector. Jahangir also gave him a mansab of Rs 400. However, he could not obtain any permanent trade concessions due to opposition from the Portuguese.

question: Who built 'Bibi Ka Maqbara' in Aurangabad?
solution: Bibi Ka Maqbara is called the 'Taj Mahal of the South' or 'a crude imitation of the Taj Mahal'. It symbolizes the declining economic condition of the Mughals and the decline of architecture as there is very little use of marble in it.

question: In which year did Aurangzeb conquer the fort of 'Golkonda' and include it in the Mughal Empire?
solution: After the victory of Golconda, the Mughals gained famous diamond mines and immense wealth. The end of the Qutb Shahi dynasty was a major success of Aurangzeb's southern campaign, but the subsequent shift of the center of administration to the south led to weakness in North India.

question: Between whom was the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) fought?
solution: The Mughal emperor at the time of the Third Battle of Panipat was Shah Alam II. This war decided that the Marathas would not rule India, which cleared the way for the British.

question: In which battle did Sher Shah Suri defeat Humayun and capture the power of Delhi?
solution: Sher Shah's strategy in the battle of Kannauj was so accurate that Humayun's huge Mughal army got scattered without any major conflict. Sher Shah then established the Second Afghan Empire by capturing Delhi and Agra.

question: On whose instructions did Humayun's sister 'Gulbadan Begum' write 'Humayunnama'?
solution: Humayunnama is the only text of the Mughal period written by a woman. It gives a very human description of the internal arrangement and family relations of the Mughal harem.

question: Where was the city of 'Din-Panaah' established during the reign of Humayun?
solution: Humayun died due to falling from the stairs of the library (Sher Mandal) of this humble refuge. Today this place is part of the 'Purana Qila' complex of Delhi.

question: Which title did Shahjahan give to his beloved daughter 'Jahanara'?
solution: Jahanara Begum was the eldest daughter of Shahjahan. He had designed Chandni Chowk of Delhi. He supported Dara Shikoh in the war of succession.

question: What did Akbar mean by the term 'Sawar' in the 'Mansabdari' system?
options: The actual number of horsemen maintained by the Mansabdar was an indicator of his military power.
The personal salary of Mansabdar was determined by the post of 'Jat'.
solution: The Mansabdari system is a proof of Akbar's administrative talent. It transformed the tribal and feudal army into a professional royal army.

question: Who drafted 'Mazhar' (1579) during the reign of Akbar?
solution: Mazhar made Akbar the final arbiter in religious matters. If there was a difference of opinion among the scholars on any religious interpretation, the emperor's decision was considered supreme. This further strengthened Akbar's political power.

question: In which year was the new religion or code of conduct called 'Deen-e-Ilahi' started by Akbar?
solution: The only Hindu who accepted Deen-e-Ilahi was Birbal. It was more of a moral code than a religion, which could not succeed after Akbar's death and gradually died out.

question: In which language is the 'Humayunnama' written by 'Gulbadan Begum' during the reign of Humayun?
solution: Humayun Nama is a very important personal account of Mughal history. It not only talks about wars, but also contains information about the social and family life of that time.

question: Which scholar brought up 'Abdul Rahim Khan-e-Khana' in Akbar's court?
solution: Akbar not only made Rahim a scholar but also gave him the post of 'Khan-i-Khana' (commander of generals). Rahim was the greatest example of Akbar's generosity.

question: Who built the famous 'Peacock Throne'?
solution: The Peacock Throne was looted and taken away by the Iranian invader Nadir Shah in 1739. Along with this he also took the Kohinoor diamond.

question: Which mosque was built by Shahjahan near the grave of his wife Mumtaz Mahal after her death?
solution: A mosque is located to the west of the main dome of the Taj Mahal so that prayers can be offered there. To balance the architecture, a 'Jawab' (a similar looking building) has also been built to its east.

question: By what name was the group under the influence of 'Noorjahan' known during the reign of Jahangir?
solution: Between 1611 and 1622, the Nur Jahan junta had complete control over Jahangir's rule. All important decisions of the court were taken by this group. Later this group broke due to Khurram's rebellion.

question: Which practice was stopped by Akbar to strengthen relations with the 'Rajputs'?
options: Akbar himself was very fond of hunting.
The practice of enslaving and converting prisoners of war
solution: Akbar realized that India could not be ruled by the power of the sword alone. He made the Rajputs his friends and made them the backbone of the Mughal army. This policy gave long stability to the Mughals in India.

question: Who kept accounts of the revenue collected by 'Aamli' in the Mughal administration?
solution: The success of the Mughal revenue system depended on this systematic record-keeping. Todar Mal had ensured that the details of each farm were recorded in government documents.

question: Which princess did Shahjahan get the main market of his capital 'Shahjahanabad' (Delhi) designed?
solution: The original design of Chandni Chowk was built along a canal, with the reflection of moonlight in the water. Jahanara's business acumen was also very good.

question: Which treaty (1665) did Aurangzeb force Shivaji Maharaj to sign?
solution: Under the Treaty of Purandar, Shivaji had to hand over 23 of his forts to the Mughals and accept to send his son Sambhaji to the Mughal court. Later Shivaji escaped from Aurangzeb's Agra jail and resumed his struggle.

question: Which part of Ibrahim Lodhi's army was first destroyed by Babar in the battle of 'Panipat'?
solution: The Indian kings' reliance on elephants proved a weakness against Babur's artillery. Ibrahim Lodhi's army suffered massive destruction due to the elephants going crazy.

question: What was Jahangir's childhood name?
solution: Jahangir ascended the throne in 1605. He has a special place in history for establishing the chain of justice and patronizing painting.

question: What was the meaning of the word 'Zat' in the 'Mansabdari' system started by Akbar?
options: The number of horsemen that had to be maintained was called 'Sawar', not caste.
Personal rank and salary of Mansabdar
solution: The Mansabdari system was introduced in 1571. Mansabdars were paid in cash or in the form of jagir. This post was not hereditary and depended on the will of the ruler.

question: In which style did Akbar build 'Jodha Bai Mahal' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
solution: Jodha Bai Mahal is the largest and important residential palace of Fatehpur Sikri. It is a symbol of Akbar's religious tolerance and his respect for different cultures.

question: What was the meaning of 'Suba' in Mughal administration?
solution: The head of each province was 'Nazim' or 'Subedar' who was appointed by the emperor. The Subedar and Diwan jointly managed the law and order and revenue in the state.

question: Who was the chief architect of Humayun's Tomb?
solution: Humayun's tomb is located in Delhi. This is the first mausoleum in India which is built in the middle of a huge garden. Its architecture laid the foundation for the future construction of the Taj Mahal.

question: In which year did Akbar shift his capital from Agra to Fatehpur Sikri?
solution: Fatehpur Sikri was the first planned capital of the Mughals. A mixture of architectural styles of Gujarat and Bengal can be seen here. Akbar later had to abandon this city due to lack of water.

question: After the death of 'Birbal' in Akbar's court, which wise courtier was considered the chief advisor in his place?
solution: Like Birbal, the personality of Mulla Do Pyaza is also very famous in folklore. He was one of Akbar's nine gems and was also a personal friend of the emperor.

question: By what name are the 'Syed brothers' (Abdullah Khan and Hussain Ali Khan) known in Mughal history?
solution: The Syed brothers had attained a very powerful position in the Mughal court, but were later eliminated by Mohammad Shah with the help of Nizam-ul-Mulk.

question: In which year did Aurangzeb re-introduce 'Jizya' tax?
solution: The reintroduction of Jizya tax created great discontent among Hindus, especially Rajputs and Marathas. This became one of the social reasons for the decline of the Mughal Empire.

question: Who was appointed by Shahjahan as the master mason for the construction of 'Taj Mahal'?
solution: Thousands of artisans from Iran, Türkiye and India participated in the construction of the Taj Mahal. The skill shown by Ustad Isa in joining and carving stones is unmatched even today.

question: Which building was built by Shahjahan in the premises of 'Taj Mahal' to maintain balance, which is called 'Jawab'?
solution: Symmetry was the most important element in Shahjahan's architecture. The entire garden of the Taj Mahal and the surrounding buildings are made in such a way that they appear to be a reflection of each other.

question: Where was the post of 'Mutasaddi' in the Mughal administration?
options: In the royal gardens, there used to be Daroga-e-Bagh.
At the village level, there used to be Muqaddam and Patwari.
In the markets of the capital, the Kotwal was the chief.
solution: Mutasaddi was responsible for the collection of custom duty and smooth running of maritime trade. Surat was the largest port of the Mughals, which was called the 'Gate of Mecca'.

question: In which year did Akbar end 'Jizya' tax?
solution: The abolition of Jizya tax was a key part of Akbar's policy of 'Sulh-i-Kul'. Due to this the Mughals got the support of Rajputs and the majority Hindu people. However, Aurangzeb re-imposed it in 1679.

question: Which important Hindu text was translated into Persian by 'Abdul Qadir Badayuni' in Akbar's court?
solution: Badayuni completed the translation of Ramayana in four years. He is more famous for his book 'Muntkhaab-ut-Tawarikh', in which he has sharply criticized the religious policies of Akbar.

question: Sher Shah Suri started using which type of 'Zarib' (rope) for measuring land revenue?
