solution: Sher Shah took measurement very seriously. He used 'Gaj-i-Sikandari' and ensured that farmers were paid tax according to the quality of their land.

question: From whom did Babur learn his war strategy 'Tulughma'?
solution: Babar was a great commander who learned even from his defeat. He created such a combination of Tulughma policy and artillery against Ibrahim Lodhi and Rana Sanga in India that he remained unbeatable.

question: On what condition did Jahangir release the king of Kishtwar after his victory?
options: He had not made any such demand on the condition of marrying his daughter.
On the condition of paying heavy taxes and accepting the subordination of the Mughals, Jahangir emphasized on subordination rather than expansion of the empire.
On the condition of changing his religion
On the condition of going to Mecca
solution: The conquest of Kishtwar was for the Mughals a symbol of their growing influence in the hill regions. Jahangir conducted several successful campaigns in Kashmir and its surrounding areas.

question: What was the main responsibility of 'Waqia-Navis' in the Mughal administration?
options: Writer of court events and news
solution: The wakia-navis were an essential part of the empire's information system. Through them the emperor came to know whether the subedars and other officers were performing their responsibilities properly or not.

question: Who built Humayun's Tomb in Delhi?
solution: Humayun's Tomb is the first tomb in India which is situated amidst a huge Charbagh style garden. It was included in the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1993.

question: In which year was 'Mazhar' (Infallibility Decree) announced during the reign of Akbar?
solution: The declaration of Mazhar was prepared by Sheikh Mubarak (father of Abul Fazal). Its objective was to reduce the power of the radical Ulemas and to make the emperor supreme.

question: Why did Akbar make 'Turkish Sultana's Palace' in 'Fatehpur Sikri' famous?
options: Because of the fine and amazing carvings done on its walls, it is also called 'stone jewellery'.
Due to its very large size
solution: The palace of the Turkish Sultana is counted among the best buildings of the Mughal period for its carvings. Its decoration has such beautiful carvings of birds, animals and flowers that it looks like wooden carvings.

question: Which Mughal princess did 'Nadir Shah' get married to his son 'Nasirullah' before leaving Delhi?
options: This marital relationship with Mohammad Shah's daughter was a way to ensure his victory and dominance over the Mughals.
Aurangzeb's daughter was not alive at that time.
solution: After this marriage, Nadir Shah declared formal friendship with the Mughals, although he plundered them completely.

question: What was the post of 'Munsif-e-Munsifan' in the administration of Sher Shah Suri?
options: The chief commander of the army was Ariz-i-Mumalik.
The head of the intelligence department was Barid-e-Mumalik.
The head of justice and civil administration at the district level
solution: Sher Shah had greatly strengthened the centralized administration. He made the judicial system so strict that it was said that "even an old woman could travel safely with a basket full of gold ornaments."

question: Humayun had divided the empire with his brothers, which area did his brother 'Askari' get?
solution: Humayun's generosity became his weakness. Askari often conspired against Humayun and when Humayun was fleeing after being defeated by Sher Shah, Askari tried to capture him instead of helping him.

question: To which foreign traveler did Jahangir offer 'Mansab' and 'Jagir' of Rs. 400?
solution: The granting of Mansab to an Englishman by Jahangir shows that the Mughals had realized the maritime power and trading capability of the British. Hawkins had learned the language and manners of the Mughal court by staying there.

question: Where did the 'Mirza' rebellion take place during Humayun's reign which troubled him a lot?
options: The influence of the Mughals had not yet started in South India.
Near Sambhal and Agra, Humayun's own relatives (Mirzas) challenged his authority.
solution: There were no fixed rules of succession among the Mughals, due to which every prince and close relative considered himself a claimant to the throne. Humayun's entire life was spent fighting these internal disputes.

question: To which musician did Akbar give the title of 'Mian'?
solution: Tansen is considered unique in the field of music. It was said about him that he could light a lamp or cause rain with his singing. He had a prominent place among the Navaratnas of Akbar.

question: In which year did Shahjahan start the construction of 'Red Fort' and 'Jama Masjid' in Delhi?
solution: The Red Fort of Delhi is famous for its grandeur and architecture. Within it there are important buildings like Diwan-i-Aam and Diwan-i-Khas. Jama Masjid is one of the largest mosques in India.

question: Who wrote about Humayun that "Humayun became free from this life by falling"?
solution: This comment of Lanepool reflects the struggle of Humayun throughout his life. He lost his throne, suffered exile, regained it and was ultimately killed in an accident.

question: Which Mughal Wazir did 'Nadir Shah' send as his messenger to Mohammad Shah after the battle of Karnal?
solution: Nizam-ul-Mulk had decided the terms of the treaty on behalf of the Mughals. However Nadir Shah later changed his terms and decided to plunder Delhi.

question: With which Mughal ruler did the British sign the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) after winning the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
solution: After the Treaty of Allahabad, the Mughal Emperor became a pensioner of the British and the power of Delhi remained nominal.

question: Who was installed on the throne by the 'King Makers' (Sayad brothers) in Mughal history?
solution: The influence of the Syed brothers had increased so much in the Mughal court that they could make whomever they wanted as emperor and remove whomever they wanted. Ultimately Mohammad Shah ousted him from power.

question: Why did Shahjahan construct 'Anguri Bagh' in 'Agra Fort'?
options: There was a place for this outside the fort as a horse stable.
solution: Khas Mahal and Sheesh Mahal were situated around Angoori Bagh. This place is a great example of the luxury and artistry of Mughal life.

question: In which war did Babar use the 'Tulughma' war policy?
solution: In the Tulughma policy, the army was divided into the main army, right and left wings so that the enemy could be surrounded from the rear. Along with this, the use of cannons made Babar invincible.

question: What was the main responsibility of 'Diwan-i-Khalsa' in the Mughal administration?
options: It was the job of Diwan-i-Taan to distribute the jagirs.
Managing the lands under royal control (Khalsa)
solution: Khalsa lands were the backbone of the Mughal economy. The emperor always tried to keep the area of ​​Khalsa land large so that he did not lack funds for his personal army and expenses.

question: Where was the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled after the rebellion of 1857?
solution: Bahadur Shah Zafar was also a famous Urdu poet. His death marked the formal end of the 300-year-old Mughal dynasty in India. The British had murdered his sons at the bloody gates of Delhi.

question: Who were the first Europeans to come for 'Company' or 'Trade' during Humayun's reign?
solution: The Portuguese had tried to form an alliance with Bahadur Shah of Gujarat against Humayun. Humayun's lack of maritime power remained a permanent weakness for the Mughals.

question: Which Sikh Guru was given death sentence by Jahangir?
solution: The martyrdom of Guru Arjun Dev changed Sikh history. After this a long series of conflicts began between the Sikhs and the Mughals and the Sikhs began to organize military power.

question: Which Mughal emperor gave the title of 'Raja' to Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
solution: The reign of Akbar II was the period of complete end of Mughal power. He was dependent only on the pension of the British and was confined to the Red Fort.

question: How did Aurangzeb treat the Sultans of Bijapur and Golkonda after conquering them?
options: Aurangzeb ended those empires but it was not his aim to kill the Sultans.
solution: The victory of these two Shia states was a major success for Aurangzeb, but after this the burden of administration increased so much that he could not handle it.

question: Which Mughal ruler built the 'Allahabad Fort'?
solution: Allahabad Fort was a major base for the Mughals to expand eastward. It is one of the largest forts built by Akbar.

question: Which war method did Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj advise King Chhatrasal to use?
solution: It was under the inspiration of Shivaji Maharaj that Chhatrasal started a rebellion against the Mughals with a small army and eventually established a powerful Hindu state in Bundelkhand.

question: Which Mughal officer was appointed by Aurangzeb as 'Sadr-us-Sudoor' to monitor religious grants?
solution: Sadr's powers greatly increased during the time of Aurangzeb as he gave huge grants to religious institutions provided they supported his hardline policies. He also canceled many old Hindu grants.

question: Which new measurement unit was introduced by Sher Shah Suri for 'land measurement'?
solution: Sher Shah measured the land and determined the tax based on its quality. He used a flax stick (Zarib) so that the measurement could not be tampered with. This brought transparency in the revenue department.

question: The 'Dahshala' system which was developed by Todarmal was mainly related to?
solution: The Dahashala system eliminated uncertainty in revenue assessment. This was a refined form of the 'Zabti' system. It provided a strong economic base to the Mughal Empire.

question: 'Battle of Ghaghra' (1529) Against which powers did Babar fight?
solution: The Battle of Ghaghra was Babur's last major battle fought on both water and land. This victory secured the borders of the Mughal Empire around Delhi and Agra. Babar died just a year later in 1530.

question: In the court of Akbar, 'Birbal' was made the vassal of which 'city'?
solution: Birbal's palace and his memories are still safe in Kalpi. He was so loyal to Akbar that he was ready to go on any military expedition for him.

question: What was the main function of 'Mir-i-Bahr' in the Mughal administration?
options: Management of Navy and River Fleet
The head of the royal gardens was called Daroga-i-Bagh.
solution: The function of Mir-i-Bahar was more important in coastal provinces like Bengal and Gujarat. He arranged ships for Hajj pilgrims and attempted to prevent piracy.

question: Along with giving the title of 'Raja', how much mansab was given to 'Birbal' in Akbar's court?
solution: Mansab was not just a military post, but it was an indicator of the dignity and salary of a courtier in the court. Birbal's mansab was a symbol of his closeness to the emperor.

question: What was the practice of paying land revenue in cash under the 'Dahshala' system in Akbar's court called?
solution: In the confiscation system, both the measurement of land and the price of crops were fixed. This system was applicable in those areas where the administrative control of the Mughals was very strong.

question: Nadir Shah's invasion (1739) took place during the reign of which Mughal ruler?
solution: Nadir Shah looted the Peacock Throne, Kohinoor diamond and immense wealth and took it to Iran. This attack exposed the hollowed out power of the Mughal Empire to the entire world.

question: Which Mughal ruler was called 'Zinda Pir' because of his simplicity and religious fanaticism?
solution: Aurangzeb led a very disciplined and simple life in his personal life, which was in sharp contrast to the luxury of other Mughal emperors.

question: Sher Shah Suri divided the 'province' of Bengal into what to stop the rebellions?
solution: Sher Shah created a new post in Bengal called 'Shikdar-e-Shikdaran' which looked after law and order only. This decentralization policy established peace in Bengal, which earlier had always been a hotbed of rebellion.

question: Akbar built 'Salim Chishti's Tomb' in 'Fatehpur Sikri', which stone was it originally made of?
solution: Sheikh Salim Chishti was the spiritual guru of Akbar. Akbar was considered to have got his children with his blessings. This tomb is still a major center of faith.

question: Which officer was held accountable for 'crime control' by Sher Shah Suri?
solution: Due to this strict policy of Sher Shah, the law and order in his kingdom was so strong that it was said that "even an old woman could travel safely with a basket of gold ornaments."

question: Which mosque was built by Shahjahan in Agra for his beloved daughter 'Jahanara'?
solution: Jahanara Begum spent her personal money for the construction of Jama Masjid of Agra. This mosque is located just opposite the railway station of Agra and is also known as 'Masjid-e-Jahanuma'.

question: Which Hindu among the 'Navratnas' was the finance minister in Akbar's court?
solution: Todar Mal got the land measured scientifically and made tax assessment transparent. His revenue policies were also later adopted by the British rule.

question: Which title did Aurangzeb hold which means 'World Conqueror'?
solution: Aurangzeb was the last great Mughal emperor. During his time the Mughal Empire reached the peak of its geographical boundaries, although his religious policies also laid the foundation for the empire's decline.

question: For what purpose did Akbar start giving high positions in the Mughal army to 'Rajputs'?
options: Akbar's policy for converting Rajputs to Islam was one of religious tolerance, not forced conversion.
To provide a permanent basis to the Mughal power in India, he understood that it was impossible to rule India for a long time without the support of Hindus (especially Rajputs).
solution: Akbar's Rajput policy was based on 'friendship and marital relations'. He gave a mansab of 7000 to Rajput kings like Raja Man Singh, which was the highest post for any non-Muslim at that time.

question: To which Mughal ruler did Queen Karnavati of Mewar ask for help by sending Rakhi?
solution: Although Humayun accepted Rakhi, he could not reach her for help in time. Due to this delay Queen Karnavati had to commit Jauhar. This incident is considered a sentimental example of Hindu-Muslim cultural relations in medieval history.

question: After which battle did Babur assume (or was called) the title of 'Qalandar'?
solution: Due to this charity of Babur, every citizen of Kabul got a silver coin (Shahrukhhi). Because of his generosity he was called 'Qalandar'.

question: At which place did Akbar's coronation take place when he was only 13 years old?
solution: Akbar's full name was Jalaluddin Mohammad Akbar. Bairam Khan was his patron during his early reign. Akbar re-established Mughal power by defeating Hemu in the second battle of Panipat in 1556.

question: Whose descendant is Babar considered to be from his paternal side?
solution: Babar had the blood of two great conquering warriors in his veins. He was the fifth descendant of Taimur from the paternal side and the fourteenth descendant of Genghis Khan from the maternal side.

question: What was the original name of 'Mian' Tansen?
solution: Tansen is considered the greatest guru of Indian classical music. Akbar had given him the title of 'Mian'. It was said about him that he could light lamps with his singing.

question: Aurangzeb had stopped the construction of which Mughal building considering it 'anti-Islam'?
options: He himself used to go to Jama Masjid there to offer namaz.
The construction of the Red Fort was completed during the time of Shahjahan.
solution: Aurangzeb was a staunch Sunni Muslim. He also stopped the practices of weighing the emperor in gold (Tuladan) and engraving Kalma on coins because he considered them un-Islamic.

question: Why did Sher Shah Suri siege the fort of 'Kalinjar'?
options: He wanted to make his capital there
He wanted to convert the Rajputs to Islam
The king there had given shelter to the Afghan rebels. Sher Shah wanted to root out the rebels.
solution: The campaign of Kalinjar proved to be the last for Sher Shah. Sher Shah was badly burnt by the explosion of a shell that returned after hitting the fort wall and died.

question: Who was the founder of the Mughal dynasty who defeated the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate in 1526?

question: During the attack of 'Nadir Shah', the Dargah of which famous Sufi saint of Delhi was also attacked?
solution: Nadir Shah's invasion was so destructive that it did not even respect religious and holy places. It shook the entire social and cultural structure of Delhi.

question: What type of land was called 'Polaj' during the Mughal period?
options: The most fertile land on which farming was done regularly
The land which was left vacant for 1-2 years to increase fertility was called 'Parauti'.
The land which was left vacant for 3-4 years was called 'Chachar'.
The worst land which was vacant for 5 or more years was called 'Banjar'.
solution: During the reign of Akbar, land was divided into four categories based on its fertility so that revenue could be determined accurately. Maximum tax was received from Polj.

question: Who gifted 'Kohinoor Diamond' to Shahjahan during his reign?
solution: Mir Jumla gave this world famous diamond to Shahjahan to win his trust. Later Shahjahan got it embedded in the Peacock Throne.

question: Which city of India has been described by Babar in his autobiography as 'very big and one of the most famous cities in the world'?
solution: Babur established Agra as the main capital of the Mughals. He built many beautiful gardens and fountains on the banks of Yamuna there so that he would not miss Kabul.

question: In the period of Jahangir, the most extensive use of 'Pietra Dura' style can be seen in which building which was built by 'Noor Jahan'?
solution: The tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula is the first Mughal building made of white marble. The inlay of gems in it is so fine that it still looks like new. Noorjahan had built it for her father.

question: What was the function of 'Aamli' or 'Amal-Gujar' officer during the Mughal period?
solution: Amal-gujar ensured that farmers had to pay taxes at fair rates and there was no theft of revenue. He enforced the rules established by Todarmal.

question: At which place was the war of succession fought between the sons of Shahjahan in which Aurangzeb was victorious?
solution: Aurangzeb gained the throne by defeating his brothers Dara Shikoh, Shuja and Murad. He imprisoned his father Shahjahan in Agra Fort, where he died in 1666.

question: Which river of India has been described by Babar as 'dirty and dangerous' in 'Baburnama'?
solution: Babur was impressed by the natural beauty of India but hated its dust, heat and some geographical areas. He has written his likes and dislikes very candidly in his book.

question: Which area did 'Nadir Shah' pretend to hand over to 'Mohammad Shah Rangeela' while returning from Delhi?
options: The entire Mughal Empire east of the Indus River accepted Mohammad Shah as the ruler again but he was practically bankrupt.
solution: Nadir Shah's main objective was not to rule India but to plunder. He limited the boundaries of the Mughal Empire to the Indus River and took control of Afghanistan and parts of north-western India.

question: By which other name was 'Ahmad Shah Abdali' known which means 'Pearl of the Age'?
solution: Abdali was the most capable commander of Nadir Shah. It was because of his military talent that an invincible power like the Marathas had to face defeat in the field of Panipat. He organized Afghanistan as a nation.

question: In which year did Akbar start the 'Mansabdari' system?
solution: The word Mansab means 'post' or 'rank'. The status of each Mansabdar was determined by 'Jat' and 'Sawar'. Caste determined his rank and salary, while rider determined the number of horsemen manning him.

question: 'Shikdar' was the officer of which administrative unit during the Mughal period?
solution: The main function of the Shikdar was to maintain peace in the Pargana and assist the 'Amil' in collecting revenue. This post was very important during the time of Sher Shah Suri.

question: What is the name of the 'fort' built by Sher Shah Suri which he built there after destroying 'Kannauj'?
solution: Sher Shah believed that destroying old monuments and building new ones was a way to show the strength of his power. Shergarh was an important part of the defense line of North India.

question: Which Sikh Guru's son 'Guru Hargobind' was put under house arrest by Jahangir in Gwalior Fort?
solution: Guru Hargobind was later released and he also freed 52 Hindu kings with him, in whose memory 'Bandi Chhod Diwas' (Deepawali day) is celebrated.

question: Which thing of India did Babur feel was lacking the most in 'Baburnama'?
options: Babur, accustomed to the cold water and good melons of the climate of Central Asia, did not like the heat of India and its fruits (except mangoes).
India had immense wealth of gold and silver, Babar praised it.
solution: Babar wrote that "India is a strange country, where there are neither good horses, nor good melons, nor ice-cold water." He made a lot of efforts to improve the rivers and gardens here.

question: What was the post of 'Mir-i-Barr' in the Mughal administration?
options: In charge of the forest and hunting department
solution: The Mughal emperors were very fond of hunting, but it was also a part of military training. Mir-i-Bar ensured that there was no damage to the environment during hunting and that the elephant population remained intact.

question: Which Mughal general was defeated by Ahom commander Lachit Borphukan in the Battle of Saraighat (1671)?
solution: The battle of Saraighat was fought on the banks of the Brahmaputra river. Due to the bravery and fighting skills of Lachit Borphukan, the Mughals had to retreat and the Ahom kingdom was successful in saving its independence.

question: In whom did 'Todarmal' serve in Akbar's court before taking charge of the Revenue Department?
solution: The secret of Todarmal's success was that he had closely observed both Afghan and Mughal administrative styles. He prepared 'Dahshala' for Akbar by making Sher Shah's measurement system more scientific.

question: 'Tansen' is most remembered for which raga in Akbar's court which was believed to be able to light a lamp?
solution: Tansen's music was not only entertainment but was also considered a spiritual practice. Akbar often went to him in disguise to listen to his singing.

question: In which part of the 'Red Fort of Delhi' did Shahjahan establish the 'Seat of Justice'?
solution: The emperor's sitting place in Diwan-i-Aam was called 'Takht-i-Murad'. The walls behind it have pietra dura work in which the Greek god 'Orpheus' is shown playing the lyre.

question: Why did Sher Shah Suri attack 'Kalinjar'?
options: The king Kirat Singh there had given shelter to the Afghan rebels. Sher Shah wanted to root out the rebels.
solution: Kalinjar fort was considered Ajay. Sher Shah lost his life in an accident during its siege. His death proved to be a boon for the Mughals.

question: Who was the Navratna of Akbar's court who translated 'Ramayana' into Persian?
solution: Akbar established a translation department (Maktab Khana) to transmit the knowledge of Indian religious texts to the Persian-speaking Mughal court. Mahabharata was translated under the name of 'Rajmnama' (Book of Wars).

question: What was the real name of 'Birbal' in Akbar's court?
solution: Birbal was one of Akbar's nine gems and his most trusted friend. He was also given the title of 'Kavipriya'. He died while fighting against the Yusufzai clan in 1586.

question: Which famous battle took place between Akbar and Maharana Pratap in 1576?
solution: Maharana Pratap's horse Chetak was martyred in the battle of Haldighati. The Mughal forces claimed victory but failed to capture Maharana Pratap or completely subjugate Mewar.

question: In which city did Shahjahan build 'Moti Masjid'?
solution: The Moti Masjid of Agra built by Shahjahan is famous for its simplicity and grandeur. It was built for the women of the royal family.

question: How many important years of his rule did Aurangzeb spend in 'South India'?
options: He remained in the South continuously for about 25 years from 1682 to 1707 and died there.
solution: Aurangzeb's southern policy has been called "his cancer" which cut off the roots of the Mughal Empire. He completely failed to suppress the Marathas.

question: What was the main function of 'Mir-i-Manzil' in the Mughal administration?
options: Arranging camps and lodging during the emperor's travels
solution: When the Mughal emperor went somewhere with his huge army, Mir-e-Manzil had to ensure that a tent city was ready there before the emperor reached there.

question: What ratio did Sher Shah Suri keep between the 'silver rupee' and the 'copper price'?
solution: Sher Shah's currency system was so systematic that it completely eliminated adulteration in coins. His name and title were inscribed on his coins in Arabic and Devanagari script.

question: In which year did Akbar end 'slavery'?
solution: The period 1562-1564 is considered the 'liberal period' of Akbar's reign. In these three years he carried out reforms that changed the image of the Mughals from that of a foreign plunderer to that of an Indian emperor.

question: Why did Shahjahan build 'Musamman Burj' in 'Agra Fort'?
solution: The irony is that Aurangzeb kept Shahjahan imprisoned in this Musamman Burj for the last 8 years of his life. From there he used to remember his wife Mumtaz while looking at the Taj Mahal.

question: Which Mughal ruler is known as 'Shahe Bekhabar'?
solution: Bahadur Shah I attempted to change some of Aurangzeb's harsh policies, but he was not entirely successful in reversing the declining state of the empire.

question: Where was the post of 'Kotwal' in the Mughal administration?
options: In the villages, Muqaddams and Chowkidars were responsible for security.
solution: Kotwal was entrusted not only with security but also with the cleanliness of the city, market control and keeping records of foreigners.

question: 'Jama Masjid' (Delhi) built by Shahjahan is made of which stone?
solution: Jama Masjid of Delhi is one of the largest mosques in India. It took about 6 years to build and was the main center of Shahjahanabad city.

question: 'Mian' Tansen was originally a musician in whose court from where Akbar had called him?
solution: Tansen's original name was Ramtanu Pandey. He had mastered Dhrupad singing. Ragas composed by him like 'Mian Ki Malhar' and 'Mian Ki Todi' are still considered the basis in the music world.

question: Sher Shah Suri died due to the explosion of which weapon during the siege of 'Kalinjar Fort'?
solution: Sher Shah died in 1545. Before hearing the news of his death he had received information about Kalinjar victory. He was a great warrior and an even greater administrator.

question: How many times did 'Ahmad Shah Abdali' attack India?
solution: Abdali's most important offensive was the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761. It is called 'Durr-e-Durrani' (Pearl of the Age). His attacks had completely destabilized the politics of North India.

question: Which foreign traveler visited India 6 times during the reign of Jahangir?
solution: Tavernier has given detailed information about the Kohinoor diamond and the Peacock Throne. He has given a very good description of India's trade and gem market.

question: Sher Shah Suri resorted to which ancient Indian principle for 'crime control'?
solution: Sher Shah believed that only the local chief knew the criminals of his village best. Due to this fear, the chief himself would get the criminals caught, which would maintain peace.

question: Against which Afghan chieftain did Babar win in the first battle of Panipat?
solution: This war that took place on 21 April 1526 is a milestone in the history of India. Despite Ibrahim Lodhi having a huge army, Babar defeated him with his artillery and military skills.

question: In which year did Jahangir ban the use of tobacco?
solution: It is an irony that Jahangir banned tobacco but he himself was a big addict of opium and alcohol. Tobacco spread very rapidly in India.

question: Who was the ruler of 'Gujarat' who gave a tough challenge to the Mughals during the reign of Humayun?
solution: Bahadur Shah attacked Chittor and took advantage of Humayun's weakness to increase his power. He was killed during a conflict with the Portuguese.

question: Which foreign ruler provided military assistance to Humayun in regaining power in India?
solution: In return for Persia's help, Humayun had promised to hand over the fort of Kandahar to the Safavids. With this military help, Humayun conquered Kabul and Kandahar and then regained Delhi in 1555.

question: What was the real name of 'Birbal' in Akbar's court?
solution: Birbal was one of Akbar's most trusted friends and nine gems. He died in 1586 while suppressing the Yusufzai rebellion, which greatly saddened Akbar.

question: 'Dashwant' and 'Basawan' were famous artists of which field in Akbar's court?
solution: Akbar had established a separate department for painting, 'Tasveer Khana'. Dashwant was the son of an ordinary Kahar, but Akbar recognized his talent and trained him and he became the greatest painter of his time.

question: Who was the Mughal emperor of India at the time of the rebellion of 1857?
solution: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal emperor. The Mughal dynasty officially ended with his death in Rangoon (Myanmar) in 1862.

question: At which place did Aurangzeb die in 1707?
solution: Aurangzeb was buried with utmost simplicity near the shrine of a Sufi saint at 'Khuldabad' near Aurangabad. With his death the decline of the Mughal Empire accelerated.

question: In which architectural style did Akbar build 'Birbal's Palace' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
solution: Birbal's palace is two-storeyed and is famous for its finely carved brackets. Akbar had built it for the residence of his dearest friend Birbal.

question: Which was the only state in 'Rajputana' that Akbar brought under Mughal subjugation not through war but through matrimonial alliance?
solution: The Kachwaha Rajputs of Amer became the most loyal allies of the Mughals. Raja Man Singh and Raja Bhagwan Das held the highest positions in Akbar's court.

question: For whom did Shahjahan build 'Nagina Masjid' in 'Agra Fort'?
options: Jama Masjid was used for its army.
solution: Nagina Masjid is situated near Machli Bhawan of Agra Fort. Its architecture is very delicate, reflecting Shahjahan's sensitivity towards women and his awareness of their religious needs.

question: From whom did Babur learn the art of placing cannons between the 'queues of vehicles' in his war strategy?
options: From the Safavids he learned better use of horsemen.
From the Mongols he learned siege techniques.
solution: In the first battle of Panipat, Babur built a strong defensive wall using about 700 carts. Due to this technique, Ibrahim Lodhi's huge army and elephants could not face Babar's artillery.

question: On which community did Aurangzeb re-impose 'Jizya' tax?
options: Jizya was also a reason for the rebellion of Rajputs but it was on the entire non-Muslim class.
Custom duty was levied only on foreign traders, not Jizya.
solution: Due to Jizya tax, Aurangzeb had to face strong opposition from the public. This made the Rajputs and Sikhs more aggressive against the Mughals.

question: Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Mughal army defending Delhi during the invasion of 'Nadir Shah'?
solution: After the death of Khan-e-Dauran, the Mughal army became completely leaderless. The Mughals had no answer to Nadir Shah's mobile cavalry and heavy guns (jambura).

question: Whom did 'Ahmad Shah Abdali' recognize as the Mughal Emperor of Delhi after the Third Battle of Panipat (1761)?
solution: The third battle of Panipat ended the power of the Marathas in North India. Abdali plundered Delhi but instead of ruling he returned, handing over power to his loyal people.

question: Which 'Maratha king' was honored by Aurangzeb by giving him the title of 'Raja' and also gave him Mansab?
solution: The relations between Aurangzeb and Shivaji had many ups and downs. Aurangzeb even called Shivaji a 'hill rat', but considering his military power he ultimately had to compromise.

question: Where was Akbar born?
solution: Akbar was born when Humayun was wandering from door to door after being defeated by Sher Shah Suri. Akbar's mother was Hamida Banu Begum. Akbar's childhood was spent in conflict, which made him a practical ruler.

question: Who built 'Itmaduddaula's Tomb' in Agra?
solution: Itamad-ud-Daula's tomb is the first building in Mughal architecture to be made entirely of white marble with extensive use of 'pietra dura' (inlay of gems).

question: At which place in Delhi did Babar get his coronation done after the victory in the first battle of 'Panipat'?
options: He went straight from the battlefield to Agra and celebrated the festival there
solution: Babar made Agra the first capital of the Mughals. He built geometrically shaped gardens on the banks of the Yamuna there because he missed the greenery and cool climate of Kabul.

question: Where did Jahangir mint coins in his name during the rebellion in 'Allahabad'?
solution: The rebellion of Salim (Jahangir) was a major political setback for Akbar. Akbar himself had to go to Allahabad with his army so that he could control his son.

question: In 'Ain-i-Akbari' the Mughal Empire is shown divided into how many provinces?
solution: Abul Fazal has given a detailed description of the history, revenue and military resources of each province in Ain-i-Akbari. Bengal, Bihar, Allahabad and Awadh were the major provinces.

question: Which two major states of South India were merged into the Mughal Empire by Aurangzeb?
solution: Aurangzeb's southern policy proved disastrous for the Mughal Empire. Although the empire expanded geographically, the treasury became empty and the administration weakened.

question: On the request of which Mughal princess did Aurangzeb expel the musicians from the court?
options: He did this not at anyone's request but because of his religious beliefs
solution: Aurangzeb had said that "the funeral procession of music should be buried so deep that its sound may never be heard again." However, most books on Indian classical music were written during his period.

question: Apart from 'Khalsa' land, which other land was surveyed by 'Todar Mal' in Akbar's court?
solution: The main reason for Todarmal's success was his detailed data collection. He kept records of each farm, which reduced the scope for corruption.

question: Which measurement unit was adopted by Sher Shah Suri for land revenue?
solution: Sher Shah got the land measured and got 'Rai' (revenue rate table) prepared. He also fixed 'Jaribana' (survey fee) to protect farmers from extortion.

question: At what level was the main post of 'Faujdar' in the Mughal administration?
options: At the government (district) level, he was the chief executive and military officer of the district.
At the Suba (province) level, there was a Subedar or Nazim.
At the Pargana level, there used to be a Shikdar.
solution: The function of the Faujdar was to suppress rebellions in his area, protect the people from robbers and help the Amil in revenue collection. He was directly answerable to the center or the Subedar.

question: Which Mughal princess was given the title of 'Sahibat-uz-Zamani' by Aurangzeb?
solution: Jahanara was a very learned and wealthy princess. He designed the famous 'Chandni Chowk' of Delhi. She was also known for her Sufi ideology.

question: Which Rajput king supported Dara Shikoh in the 'War of Succession' during the time of Aurangzeb?
solution: Aurangzeb later forgave Jaswant Singh and made him the Subedar of Kabul, but Aurangzeb's distrust towards him always remained.

question: Which person's invitation did Babur accept to attack India?
solution: Due to Ibrahim Lodhi's harsh and abusive policies, his own relatives and governors turned against him. They saw Babar as an opportunity, but instead of plundering India, Babar settled here.

question: At which place did Akbar establish 'Ibadat Khana'?
solution: Initially only Sunni scholars came to Ibadat Khana, but later Akbar also opened it to Hindu, Jain, Christian and Parsi scholars, which led to the development of his liberal policy.

question: At which place did 'Birbal' die in Akbar's court?
solution: Birbal's death was a personal loss for Akbar. She mourned for several days and said that "Birbal had never made my heart sad."

question: Who was the author of 'Akbarnama'?
solution: Akbarnama is divided into three parts. Its third part is called 'Ain-i-Akbari', which contains a detailed statistical description of the Mughal administration, army and economy.

question: On whose instigation was the famous scholar of Akbar's court 'Abul Fazal' murdered?
solution: In 1602, Raja Veer Singh Bundela of Orchha killed Abul Fazal at the behest of Salim. Akbar was so saddened by this news that he did not allow Salim to appear before him for several days.

question: 'Dahshala' revenue system was the gift of which minister of Akbar?
solution: In the Dahashala system, revenue was decided on the basis of the average production of the last 10 years. This freed the farmers from uncertainty and also increased the state's revenue.

question: In which year did 'Kandahar' go out of the hands of the Mughals forever during the reign of Shahjahan?
solution: The loss of Kandahar was a major strategic defeat for the Mughal Empire. This weakened the security of the north-western frontier and dented the military prestige of the Mughals.

question: At which place did Aurangzeb build his first capital where he was crowned again?
solution: Aurangzeb built 'Moti Masjid' in the Red Fort of Delhi so that he could offer namaz inside the palace itself. He kept Delhi as the main center of his administration.

question: For what special purpose did Akbar build 'Birbal's Palace' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
options: To keep the treasure safe, there was a separate building called 'Treasury'.
For the residence of Birbal and for the entertainment of the royal ladies
solution: Birbal's palace is famous for its two-storey structure and carved brackets. This is one of the most ornate palaces of Fatehpur Sikri, which shows Akbar's special attachment towards Birbal.

question: In which war did Babar raise the slogan of 'Jihad' against the Rajputs and after victory, assumed the title of 'Ghazi'?
solution: Before the battle of Khanwa, Babar's army was scared because the stories of bravery of Rajputs were famous. Babar broke the liquor vessels and made the soldiers swear to fight by placing their hands on the Quran. This emotional move changed the course of the war.

question: During the reign of which Mughal emperor did Nadir Shah invade India (1739)?
solution: Nadir Shah is called 'Napoleon of Iran'. He looted the Peacock Throne and the Kohinoor diamond and took it with him. This attack completely destroyed the remaining power of the Mughal Empire.

question: Who was the Finance Minister among the 'Navratnas' of Akbar's court who started the 'Dahshala' system?
solution: Todarmal got the land measured accurately and divided the land into four parts (Polaj, Paroti, Chachar, Banjar) on the basis of fertility. His revenue system was so effective that later the British also used it as their basis.

question: Which 'Mughal officer' was given the responsibility of demolishing temples and stopping the construction of new ones by Aurangzeb?
solution: Aurangzeb had issued a decree in 1669 under which the repair of old temples and construction of new temples was banned. Based on the reports of the witnesses, many temples were damaged.

question: In which language did the famous poet of Akbar's court 'Faizi' translate the love story of 'Nal-Damayanti'?
solution: Faizi was a great scholar who received the title of 'Malik-ush-Shuara' (King of Poets). As the head of Akbar's translation department, he played a big role in spreading Indian knowledge to the world.

question: Who did the first (incomplete) Persian translation of 'Baburnama' during the reign of Humayun?
solution: The Mughals were proud of their Turkish heritage, but they wanted to translate the literature of their ancestors into Persian, as Persian was the main language of the court.

question: Akbar's last military campaign (1601) was against which fort?
solution: After the conquest of Asirgarh, Akbar strengthened Mughal influence in South India. Akbar died in 1605 and was buried at Sikandra near Agra.

question: Which foreign power did Aurangzeb take help from to strengthen the 'Mughal Navy'?
solution: The biggest weakness of the Mughals was their navy. Aurangzeb made Siddis his 'admirals' so that they could protect maritime trade and Haj pilgrims.

question: In how many parts was the land divided in the 'Dahshala' system introduced by Akbar?
solution: Polj was the land that was cultivated every year. Parauti was left vacant for one or two years. Chachar was kept empty for three-four years and banjar for five or more years. The tax rate on each was different.

question: Along with the 'Jizya' tax, Aurangzeb also banned which festivals of Hindus?
solution: Aurangzeb had also stopped Jharokha Darshan, Tuladan (weighing the emperor in gold and silver) and engraving Kalma on coins because he considered them anti-Islamic.

question: In which language did Jahangir write his autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri'?
solution: Jahangir's autobiography honestly highlights his justice, love for nature and various aspects of his personality. It is an important primary source of Mughal history.

question: At which place during Humayun's reign did 'Kamram Mirza' betray him when he was fighting the Afghans?
options: On the border of Lahore and Punjab, Kamran had refused to provide supplies and Kumuk to Humayun's army.
Akbar was born here in Amarkot.
solution: Kamran's betrayal became the main reason for Humayun's downfall. He waited for Humayun's defeat so that he could become emperor himself, but ultimately he too failed.

question: Which poet among Akbar's 'Navratnas' was the brother of Abul Fazal, the author of 'Akbarnama'?
solution: Both Abul Fazal and Faizi were sons of the famous scholar Sheikh Mubarak. Faizi had translated 'Lilavati' (mathematical treatise) into Persian. He was a staunch supporter of Akbar's religious policies.

question: Who among Akbar's Navaratnas composed 'Akbarnama'?
solution: Akbarnama is divided into three parts. Its third and most important part is called 'Ain-i-Akbari', which contains statistical details of the Mughal administration, army and revenue system.

question: Who among Akbar's Navaratnas was given the title of 'Kavipriya'?
solution: Akbar liked Birbal very much because of his versatile talent. His poems were often based on justice and wisdom. He was Akbar's companion in entertainment as well as in serious administrative work.

question: With what type of material did Akbar construct 'Panch Mahal' in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
solution: There are a total of 176 pillars in Panch Mahal. This building is in the shape of a pyramid and each floor becomes smaller than the one below.

question: The battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between whom?
solution: Maharana Pratap did not surrender in the battle of Haldighati and continued fighting from the Aravali hills. Maharana Pratap was a Sisodiya Rajput of Mewar whose capital was Chittor.

question: Why did Sher Shah Suri build 'Rohtasgarh Fort' (on the north-west border)?
options: To control the Ghakkhar tribes and prevent the Mughals, it was a strategic fort that protected the entry route to India.
solution: Sher Shah spent a lot of money to secure the north-west frontier. He knew that Humayun could return at any time via the north-west.

question: In which year did Aurangzeb re-introduce 'Jizya' tax?
solution: The reintroduction of Jizya tax greatly deteriorated the Mughals' relations with the Rajputs and Marathas. This led to a spate of rebellions within the empire and also increased the economic burden.

question: Which building did Akbar build near the 'Dargah of Salim Chishti' located in 'Fatehpur Sikri' where he used to listen to Sufi music?
solution: Akbar was a big follower of the Chishti sect. He often went to Sikri barefoot. Mehfil Khana featured qawwalis and Sufi singing, which promoted musical coordination during the Mughal period.

question: Which Rajput ruler was defeated by Babar in the battle of Khanwa?
solution: The battle of Khanwa was more difficult than Panipat. Rana Sanga was an experienced warrior. Babur vowed to give up alcohol to boost the morale of his army and named the war as Jihad. After the victory he assumed the title of Ghazi.

question: After the death of Aurangzeb, who ascended the throne in the name of 'Bahadur Shah I'?
solution: Bahadur Shah I adopted a more liberal policy than his father. He freed Sahu ji (Maratha) from captivity and also made a peace agreement with the Rajputs. He was also called 'Shahe Bekhabar'.

question: What was the main function of 'Diwan-i-Tan' in the Mughal administration?
options: It was the job of the Qazi to administer justice.
Managing the Jagir and Cash Salaries
solution: Diwan-i-Tan was a high official of the revenue department. His job was to ensure that any officer was paid appropriately according to his position. He worked under Diwan-i-Ala (Wazir).

question: After the attack of 'Nadir Shah', which area of ​​the Mughal Empire was lost forever?
options: Area west of the Indus River (Afghanistan and North-West Frontier)
solution: The capture of the North-West Frontier by Nadir Shah again opened the doors of India to foreign invaders. After this, Abdali repeatedly attacked India.

question: What condition did 'Nadir Shah' set to stop the massacre in Delhi?
options: Nadir Shah sheathed his sword only after Mohammad Shah pleaded for forgiveness and paid heavy compensation.
solution: Thousands of people of Delhi were killed in the massacre of Nadir Shah. He looted the city to such an extent that there was silence in the streets of Delhi and the reputation of the Mughal Empire was ruined.

question: Why did Aurangzeb appoint officers called 'Muhtasib'?
options: To monitor public morality and observance of Islamic laws
It was the duty of the Faujdars to suppress the rebellions.
solution: The function of the muhtasibs was also to monitor the markets and ensure that the standards of weights and measures were correct. Aurangzeb had increased their power to ban liquor, gambling and music.

question: To commemorate which victory did Akbar start the construction of 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
options: Akbar laid the foundation of this new city after the successful campaigns of Chittor and Ranthambore conquest of 1568-69.
solution: Fatehpur Sikri is a symbol of Akbar's architectural taste and religious tolerance. Here is the shrine of Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti, from whom Akbar got his son Salim (Jahangir).

question: Who was the first English traveler to come to Jahangir's court?
solution: William Hawkins was given the title of 'English Khan' by Jahangir and a mansab of 400. However, he was not successful in obtaining trade concessions due to opposition from the Portuguese.

question: At which place did Aurangzeb die in 1707?
solution: Aurangzeb was buried in the premises of the shrine of a Sufi saint at 'Khuldabad' near Aurangabad. His grave is extremely simple, as he himself had wished.

question: What is the meaning of the word 'Humayun'?
solution: Humayun divided the empire with his brothers Kamran, Hindal and Askari, which is considered his biggest political mistake because they did not support him in times of crisis.

question: What was mainly used to deliver messages in the 'postal system' started by Sher Shah Suri?
solution: Sher Shah's postal system was so fast that news from Bengal reached Delhi in a very short time. This system was so effective that later the British also followed it.

question: During Humayun's exile, when he was at the Safavid court of Iran, he developed a special interest in which art?
solution: Humayun may not have been a successful general, but his contribution in the field of art is important. During his stay in Iran, he understood the nuances of Persian painting, which later emerged as the Mughal style combined with Indian elements.

question: Where was Akbar the governor at the time of Humayun's death?
solution: The news of Humayun's death was kept secret for some time so that Akbar could safely reach Kalanaur and be crowned.

question: Which mosque was built by Shahjahan in 'Agra' which is also known as 'Masjid-e-Jahannuma'?
solution: Jama Masjid of Agra is famous for its unique dome and architecture. It is an excellent example of cultural coordination and splendor of the Mughal period.

question: On what condition did 'Nadir Shah' give permission to the Mughals to rule while leaving Delhi?
options: On the condition of adopting Christianity
On the condition of moving the capital to Lahore
The Mughals practically became his taxpayers on the condition of paying him an annual tax (Khiraj).
On the condition of disbanding the Mughal army, the army had already been destroyed.
solution: Nadir Shah's invasion emptied the Mughal treasury and reduced their military power to naught. After this the Mughals remained only the Nawabs of Delhi.

question: Who was the first British envoy to come to Jahangir's court (1608)?
solution: William Hawkins could speak Turkish, which impressed Jahangir. However, he could not initially get trade concessions due to Portuguese influence.

question: In which year did Babar conquer Kabul?
solution: Babar's early life was a struggle. After becoming the ruler of Fargana in 1494, he had to abdicate his throne because of the Uzbegs. Ultimately in 1504 he conquered Kabul, from where he launched his campaigns towards India.

question: Which ancient book of mathematics was translated into Persian by 'Faizi', the famous scholar of Akbar's court?
solution: Faizi was the royal poet (Poet Laureate) of Akbar. He wrote many important works not only on mathematics but also on literature and philosophy. He was the elder brother of Abul Fazal.

question: Who built 'Itmaduddaula's Tomb' in Agra?
solution: It is the first building of the Mughal period made entirely of white marble. In this, 'Pietra Dura' (inlay of precious stones on marble) was used on a large scale for the first time.

question: Which famous gate was built by Akbar in 'Fatehpur Sikri'?
solution: Buland Darwaza is made of red and yellow sandstone. It is counted among the tallest and grandest gateways in the world, which shows the excellence of the architectural art of the Mughals.

question: Which Sikh Guru was given death sentence by Jahangir?
solution: Guru Arjun Dev had compiled Adi Granth. His martyrdom marked a new turn in the history of Sikhism and soured the relations of the Sikhs with the Mughals.

question: Who led the British at the time of 'Treaty of Allahabad' (1765)?
solution: The Treaty of Allahabad established the British as a political power in India. After this treaty, the Mughal Emperor remained only a pensioner of the British.

question: Which stone was used by Shahjahan in the construction of 'Diwan-i-Khas' in 'Agra Fort'?
solution: It was in Diwan-i-Khas that Shah Jahan used to meet important foreign guests. Its roof was once covered with silver, which was later removed by the Marathas and the British.

question: Which Mughal officer sacrificed his life during the attack of 'Nadir Shah' but faced Nadir Shah?
solution: The death of Khan-i-Dauran was a major blow to the Mughals as he was the main pillar of the army. After his death there was panic in the Mughal army.

question: What was the main reason given by Aurangzeb for re-introduction of 'Jizya' tax?
options: Establishing the supremacy of Islamic law over non-Muslims
solution: The Jaziya tax completely destroyed the trust of the Hindu people towards the Mughals and gave rise to many regional rebellions.

question: Which Rajput princess did Akbar marry who was later called 'Mariam-uz-Zamani'?
solution: This marriage was not just a political alliance, but it brought about revolutionary changes in the Rajput policy of the Mughals. This queen gave birth to the Mughal successor Jahangir (Salim).

question: Who was the chief architect of Taj Mahal?
solution: Construction of the Taj Mahal began in 1632 and was completed in approximately 22 years. It is made of white Makrana marble and has the status of UNESCO World Heritage Site.

question: In which year did Jahangir ascend the Mughal throne?
solution: Jahangir means 'world conqueror'. His reign is known in Mughal history for justice, the development of painting, and the political influence of Nur Jahan.

question: What was approximately the total number of roadside 'Sarais' built by Sher Shah Suri?
solution: In each Sarai there were separate food and bedding arrangements for Hindus and Muslims. These sarais gave new impetus to trade and communication within the empire.

question: In which year did 'Ahmad Shah Abdali' launch his first attack on India?
solution: Abdali's invasions further accelerated the decline of the Mughal Empire. He plundered Punjab and Delhi several times and weakened the Marathas.
